stories.headline: Israeli strikes kill 10 in Gaza; ministry says 16 schoolchildren killed in November
stories.dek: Gaza's education ministry says three attacks on students in under 24 hours raised the month's toll, as strikes continue despite the ceasefire.
stories.summary: Five Israeli strikes and a shooting killed 10 Palestinians across Gaza overnight and on Thursday, hospital officials said. Gaza's education ministry says at least 16 schoolchildren have been killed since the start of November.
body: Five Israeli strikes and a shooting overnight and on Thursday killed 10 Palestinians across Gaza, officials at Shifa and Al-Aqsa Martyrs hospitals said.

The deaths came more than a year after a ceasefire deal between Israel and Hamas, yet near-daily Israeli fire and airstrikes have continued. Families in Gaza also face shortages of food, water and shelter as winter begins.

A strike on a residential apartment in Deir Al-Balah, central Gaza, killed a man and his wife, the officials said. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defence Minister Israel Katz said in a joint statement that the military killed Khaled Abu Nada in the overnight strike. They described him as the man who oversaw economic and education affairs for Hamas in Gaza. Gaza's education ministry describes Abu Nada as its undersecretary.

Shifa hospital officials said seven more people died in three other strikes, in Gaza City and Deir Al-Balah. At Al-Aqsa Martyrs hospital, officials said a man was killed near the yellow line, which divides the territory into zones held by Hamas and by Israel.

Residents in eastern Gaza City said the Israeli military warned them to flee on Thursday evening, minutes before a building and nearby homes were struck. The military said one strike targeted three militants and gave no further detail. It did not immediately comment on the other strikes, the shooting or the warnings.

On Wednesday, Gaza's education ministry said students had been targeted "for the third time in less than 24 hours" and that the number of schoolchildren killed since the start of November had risen to 16. The ministry said two sisters, Yusra, 15, and Jana Abu al-Ouf, 13, died in an airstrike on an apartment in western Gaza City. It said their parents were also killed. The ministry said the father was a director of internal security services for Hamas in northern Gaza.

Earlier in the month, Mohammed Nidal Barbakh, 15, was shot on November 6 in al-Mawasi, Khan Younis. His father, Dr Nidal Mohammed Barbakh, said a tank fired two rounds towards a sports pitch and one ricocheted and struck his son. On November 13, shelling in Deir al-Balah killed a father, his 12-year-old son Ahmed Abu Daher, and a woman.

The Israel Defense Forces said it lacked the information needed to respond on the deaths of Ahmed and Mohammed. For the day Ahmed died, it said its operations killed "10 terrorists" and that steps were taken beforehand to reduce harm to civilians.

Gaza's health ministry says at least 74,746 Palestinians have been killed in the war and more than 20,000 of them were children. The ministry is part of the Hamas-led government. Its casualty records are seen as generally reliable but do not separate civilians from militants.
keyFacts: Gaza's health ministry puts the war's death toll at at least 74,746 Palestinians.
Unicef says 98% of school buildings in Gaza have been damaged.
Gaza's health ministry issued a meningitis epidemic alert on Tuesday, citing more than 270 new cases in October.
Hamas is weighing its response to the strikes, France 24 reported.
stories.background: The story so far: Israel and Hamas agreed a ceasefire more than a year ago, but Israeli strikes and fire in Gaza have continued almost daily. Hamas has governed Gaza since 2007. Gaza's health ministry says at least 74,746 people have been killed in more than three years of war. Israel says it targets militants and takes steps to limit civilian harm. Palestinian officials say civilians, including children and education workers, are being hit.

stories.headline: UK net migration falls to 77,000, lowest since 1997 outside the pandemic
stories.dek: The Office for National Statistics said about 85,000 Indians left the UK in the year to June 2026, the largest group of emigrants from outside the EU and nearby countries.
stories.summary: UK net migration fell to 77,000 in the year to June 2026, down from 204,000 a year earlier, official figures showed. Indians, mostly students and workers, were the biggest group of people leaving, at about 85,000.
body: Net migration to the United Kingdom fell to 77,000 in the year ending June 2026, its lowest level since 1997 apart from the Covid pandemic period, official figures released on Thursday showed.

The numbers matter in India because Indians are among the biggest groups both coming to and leaving the UK. The Office for National Statistics (ONS) said Indian was the most common non-EU+ nationality among people emigrating.
Net migration is the gap between the number of people moving to the UK and the number moving out. The latest figure is provisional and compares with 204,000 the year before.

The ONS said 55,000 Indians holding student visas and 28,000 holding work visas left the UK in the year to June 2026. A further 2,000 were logged under other visa categories, bringing the Indian total to 85,000. Chinese nationals were second, at 51,000.

Indians also remained among the largest groups arriving. The UK granted 77,000 study visas and 40,000 work visas to Indian nationals. The fall in net migration has been led by people from countries outside the European Union, including India, China, Nigeria and Pakistan.
Overall, immigration fell by 155,000, from 893,000 to 738,000. Emigration fell by 28,000, from 689,000 to 661,000.

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said the government had "restored control". She said net migration was down 92 per cent from its peak under the previous government. "This didn't happen by accident," she said. "But we won't stop here."

The Home Office also released figures for the year to September 2026. It said 31,000 people were detected arriving in the UK illegally, and 86 per cent of them came in small boats across the English Channel.
keyFacts: Immigration to the UK fell from 893,000 to 738,000 in the year to June 2026.
Emigration fell from 689,000 to 661,000 over the same period.
Home Office detected 31,000 illegal arrivals in the year to September 2026.
Small boats across the Channel accounted for 86 per cent of illegal arrivals.
Chinese nationals were the second-largest group of emigrants, at 51,000.
stories.background: Successive British governments have tried to cut legal and illegal immigration after a public backlash over its scale and the pressure on the economy. The ONS has recorded a downward trend in net migration since figures published in November 2025.

stories.headline: China reserves right to retaliate as Asian partners push back on new US tariffs
stories.dek: Singapore, Japan, India and Malaysia reject the US finding of excess industrial capacity, while Vietnam and Thailand press for trade deals to lower the proposed rates.
stories.summary: China said on Thursday it reserves the right to take "necessary measures" after the US proposed new tariffs of up to 20 per cent on its goods. Several Asian economies disputed Washington's findings and sought talks to limit the impact.
body: China said on Thursday it reserves the right to take "necessary measures" after the United States proposed new tariffs of up to 20 per cent on Chinese goods.

The proposals cover 14 trading partners, including China, the European Union, Japan and India. They matter to Asian exporters because the US is a major market, and final rates could change depending on trade deals and talks with Washington.

Chinese commerce ministry spokesman He Yadong told a regular briefing that citing "overcapacity", meaning factories producing more than markets need, was a "pretext for protectionism". He urged Washington to "return to the right track of resolving issues through dialogue and consultation".

US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told CNBC the new levies fall within the bounds of existing trade negotiations with Beijing. He said the US was offering exemptions on about US$30 billion of Chinese goods.

The duties will not take effect immediately. A public hearing is scheduled for January 25. The US-China trade truce is due to expire on January 10. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping met last week at the APEC summit in Shenzhen and are due to meet again at a G20 summit in the US in December.

Singapore said it disagreed with the findings and was "very disappointed". Its trade ministry said the country's policies "do not protect our domestic market or subsidise manufacturing for export". Singapore faces a proposed rate of up to 20 per cent and will submit comments during the consultation period.
Japan, facing a proposed 15 per cent rate, called the move "regrettable". Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara said Japan has no structural excess production capacity.

India said it has no structural excess capacity in any sector and wants an "early conclusion" of a trade agreement with the US. Washington has proposed 17 per cent on Indian goods if a deal is finalised and 25 per cent if talks fail.

Vietnam, which faces a maximum of 35 per cent that could fall to 20 per cent with a deal, said it is working to finalise an agreement quickly. It expects a final decision in February or March. Malaysia rejected the excess-capacity finding and will seek to keep its rate at or below 19 per cent.

Thailand said its proposed ceiling of 18 per cent was in line with expectations, but it would seek a lower final rate. Indonesia said it was reviewing its proposed rate of up to 18 per cent and would coordinate with affected industries.
Brazil, also facing higher US tariffs, said it would "not yield to this kind of threat".
keyFacts: The US proposed rates of between 20 per cent and 40 per cent as headline levels for 14 trading partners.
Vietnam faces up to 35 per cent, reducible to 20 per cent with a trade deal.
Malaysia wants its overall Section 301 tariff rate capped at 19 per cent.
Thailand and Indonesia each face a proposed rate of up to 18 per cent.
The US-China trade truce is due to expire on January 10.
stories.background: The story so far: The US Supreme Court struck down President Trump's sweeping global tariffs in February, ruling he lacked authority to impose them by declaring an economic emergency. The administration then opened Section 301 investigations, which allow tariffs against unfair trade practices, and launched them in March. On Wednesday the US Trade Representative proposed new duties on 14 economies after an eight-month probe into alleged excess production. The EU and China rejected the allegations. On Thursday, Asian governments and China responded.
stories.whatNext: A public hearing on the proposed tariffs is scheduled for January 25, ahead of the US-China truce expiry on January 10 and final decisions expected in February or March for some economies.

stories.headline: Trump calls revised US GDP data 'fake' and demands an investigation
stories.dek: The president said the earlier 3.4% growth estimate, issued before the midterms, was a purposeful error. Economists note that such revisions are routine as more data arrives.
stories.summary: President Donald Trump demanded an investigation after the Commerce Department revised US third-quarter growth up to 4.3% from 3.4%. He called the earlier figure fake and deliberate, and offered no evidence.
body: US President Donald Trump on Thursday demanded an immediate investigation into what he called a purposeful error in the government's earlier estimate of third-quarter economic growth.

The claim concerns the most-watched measure of the US economy. On Wednesday, the Commerce Department's Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) revised growth for July to September to an annualised 4.3%, up from the advance estimate of 3.4% issued on October 29.

Trump wrote on Truth Social that the numbers published before the election were "FAKE". "Why wasn't the correct number issued before the Election? I am asking for an immediate investigation of this situation. This is not a small error, this is a massive, and purposeful, error," he wrote. He offered no evidence. His party lost heavily in the November 3 midterms, when Democrats won both chambers of Congress and several governorships.

The BEA publishes GDP in stages. Early figures rely on partial survey data and are updated as more responses come in. The agency has said advance estimates lack complete data on inventories, trade and consumer spending on services. It did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

A May article co-written by BEA Director Vipin Arora found that estimates released 90 days after the first one have differed by about 0.52 percentage points on average this century. The latest revision was 0.9 points. CNBC's analysis found it was the largest since the second quarter of 2020, but not a record, and about double the average revision since 1990.
White House spokesman Matthew Middleton told CNBC the upward revision showed Trump's policies were "delivering results" that defy expectations.

The same release showed inflation picking up. The personal consumption expenditures price index, a gauge the US Federal Reserve watches, rose at an annual rate of 3.8% in October. In the AP Voter Poll during the midterms, 76% of voters rated the economy "not so good" or "poor".

Jim Baird, chief investment officer at Plante Moran Financial Advisors, said the data showed a resilient economy that also strengthens the case for further Fed rate rises. Traders are pricing in a nearly 100% chance of a hike at the Fed's December meeting, according to the CME FedWatch tool.
keyFacts: The advance Q3 estimate came on October 29, days before the November 3 election.
The PCE price index rose at an annual rate of 3.8% in October.
The 0.9-point revision was the largest since 1.2 points in the second quarter of 2020.
Traders see a near-certain Fed rate hike at the December meeting, per CME FedWatch.
stories.background: In August 2025, Trump dismissed the head of the Bureau of Labor Statistics after a weak jobs report, calling the data "phony" and "rigged". He has often questioned federal economic figures that were unfavourable to his administration, without providing evidence of interference.
stories.whatNext: The Federal Open Market Committee meets in December, when traders expect a rate hike.

stories.headline: IT employees' body asks government for policy on AI-related job losses
stories.dek: NITES wants companies to disclose layoffs attributed to AI, give notice and severance, and offer reskilling before cutting posts.
stories.summary: The Nascent Information Technology Employees Senate has asked for a policy framework to protect IT and ITeS workers from job losses linked to AI and automation. A separate Zoho-LinkedIn report found only 6% of Indian small and medium businesses have AI literacy across their workforce.
body: The Nascent Information Technology Employees Senate (NITES), a union-style forum of tech workers, has asked the government to frame a policy that shields staff in IT and IT-enabled services (ITeS) firms from job losses caused by artificial intelligence (AI) and automation.
The demand matters to people working in a sector where companies are adopting AI tools. NITES wants firms to disclose layoffs they attribute to such technology.
In its view, workers and government officials should be told the number of people affected, the reason their roles are ending and how many jobs technology is directly replacing.

NITES also asked companies to give reasonable advance notice, pay fair severance and clear all statutory and contractual dues. It wants firms to try upskilling and redeploying staff before they remove positions.

NITES president Harpreet Singh Saluja said in a statement: "Companies should be free to adopt new technologies and improve their productivity. However, they must also take responsibility for the employees whose livelihoods are affected by these decisions."
The body said reskilling must be "meaningful and outcome-oriented". Offering access to online courses or training material alone, it said, cannot count as adequate support.

NITES also asked the government to talk with Nasscom, the IT industry association, along with IT companies and employee representatives. It said this would help build a common framework that balances technological innovation and industry growth.

Separately, a joint report by Zoho and LinkedIn found that 6% of small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs) in India have AI literacy across their workforce, against 18% of large enterprises. LinkedIn data showed 16% of Indian SMBs have in-house AI engineering capability, against more than 34% of large firms.

The report said SMBs are cautious about sending sensitive data to AI providers. Some early adopters use bring-your-own-key setups, in which a firm connects its own AI model so that use stays within its existing contracts and data policies.
Kumaresh Pattabiraman, LinkedIn's India country manager, said: "The next step is to make AI a skill for every employee, not a specialist skill for a few."
keyFacts: The Zoho-LinkedIn report says AI-assisted search among SMBs on Zoho Workplace has roughly doubled.
Use of password management tools by SMBs rose by about 35%, the report said.
The Economic Survey 2025-26 puts SMBs at about 31% of India's GDP and nearly 49% of exports.
In the 12 months to June 2026, SMB sellers using AI did roughly 40% more sales activity, LinkedIn data shows.
stories.background: Employee groups have in recent days sought common rules on AI-related job losses. Nasscom has separately asked the government for a three-year scheme in Budget 2027-28 to help IT firms move to AI-led services. Pre-Budget submissions are proposals, not commitments.

stories.headline: New survey finds 56% of women aged 15-49 anaemic; Andhra Pradesh elderly women worst hit
stories.dek: The ICMR survey shows 81.7% of Andhra Pradesh women aged 60 and above are anaemic, while experts say it cannot be compared with earlier national surveys.
stories.summary: A new ICMR survey released on November 24 found nearly 56% of Indian women aged 15-49 anaemic. In Andhra Pradesh, 81.7% of women aged 60 and above are anaemic, the highest among states surveyed.
body: The Indian Council of Medical Research released a national survey on November 24. It found that about 56% of women aged 15-49 in India are anaemic.
In Andhra Pradesh, 81.7% of women aged 60 and above have the condition. That is the highest rate among the states surveyed.

Anaemia means too few red blood cells or too little haemoglobin to carry oxygen well. The figures bear on Anaemia Mukt Bharat, the government programme begun in 2018 to cut anaemia among children, adolescents and women, mainly through iron and folic acid supplements.

The survey, called SAMPADA, was run by ICMR and its National Institute of Nutrition between 2023 and 2025. It covered more than two lakh people from over 81,000 households in 183 districts across 35 states and Union Territories. More than 1.7 lakh blood samples were analysed.
Nationally, 41.8% of children aged 12-59 months and 46.3% of girls aged 10-19 were anaemic. The rate was 22-23% among boys aged 10-19 and men aged 20-59.

Andhra Pradesh stood above the national average in most groups. Some 68.5% of women aged 15-49 were anaemic, against 55.9% nationally. Among children aged 12-59 months, the state figure was 57.5%, against 41.8%.
Among men aged 60 and above the state figure was 62.5%, against 44.7%. For men aged 20-59 it was 21.3%, slightly below the national 22%.

Kerala recorded the lowest prevalence in seven of nine categories. West Bengal had the highest rate among women of reproductive age, at 72.4%. Uttarakhand had the lowest among elderly women, at 31.6%.

The Union Health Ministry said in a statement that the shift was encouraging and that severe anaemia was seen in under 2% of people in most age groups. Dr Rajiv Bahl, ICMR Director General and Secretary of the Department of Health Research, said lower prevalence than in earlier surveys gave an evidence base to strengthen national efforts.

Experts say the results cannot be set beside the National Family Health Survey (NFHS). SAMPADA drew venous blood from a vein, while NFHS used finger-prick tests. It also defined adolescents as aged 10-19, against 15-19 in NFHS.
Public health expert Dr Sylvia Karpagam said SAMPADA's sample was small and called the removal of anaemia data from NFHS deliberate. The government has said finger-prick tests overstated anaemia.

A Lok Sabha reply in March 2026 showed Anaemia Mukt Bharat spent over Rs 2,534.97 crore from 2021-22 to 2024-25. Spending was 73.23% of approved funds in 2021-22 and 33.76% the next year. In 2024-25 it was 38.93% of Rs 809 crore. The average utilisation rate was 52.82%.
keyFacts: SAMPADA used 1.7 lakh blood samples from over 81,000 households in 183 districts.
Andhra Pradesh: 57.5% of children aged 12-59 months anaemic, against 41.8% nationally.
Anaemia Mukt Bharat's average fund utilisation was 52.82%, a gap of Rs 2,264.43 crore.
The NFHS-6 factsheet released in May omitted anaemia data.
stories.background: NFHS-4 recorded anaemia in 53.2% of women aged 15-49; NFHS-5 found 57%, drawing criticism of Anaemia Mukt Bharat and Poshan Abhiyaan. The government then dropped anaemia figures from NFHS-6, saying finger-prick tests overestimated prevalence. SAMPADA is the first national release since.

stories.headline: 91 mm rain in an hour floods Thiruvananthapuram; yellow alert for nine districts
stories.dek: Roads to the Thampanoor railway station and bus stand went under water on Thursday, and the IMD's yellow alert for Friday covers six districts.
stories.summary: East Fort in Thiruvananthapuram recorded 91 mm of rain in 60 minutes on Thursday, flooding roads and stranding commuters. The IMD issued a yellow alert for nine Kerala districts, and the state's Home Minister and the BJP-run city corporation differ over preparedness.
body: East Fort in Thiruvananthapuram recorded 91 mm of rain in 60 minutes on Thursday, 26 November, flooding roads in the city centre and stranding hundreds of commuters.
The water submerged roads leading to the Thampanoor railway station and the KSRTC bus stand. Commuters had to wade through knee-deep, dirty water to reach their trains and buses.

Several parked cars and two-wheelers were partly under water. Garbage and plastic waste from the Amayizhanchan canal washed onto the roads. Traffic police diverted light vehicles and let only buses use the flooded stretches.

Water took about two hours to recede after the rain stopped. Television visuals showed people sitting on roadside barricades waiting for it to go down. Police officers cleared drain inlets near Thampanoor station by hand and with sticks.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued a yellow alert on Thursday for nine districts: Thiruvananthapuram, Kollam, Pathanamthitta, Alappuzha, Kottayam, Ernakulam, Idukki, Malappuram and Kozhikode.

For Friday, the alert covers six districts: Kottayam, Ernakulam, Idukki, Malappuram, Kozhikode and Wayanad. The IMD forecast thunderstorms with lightning and winds of 30–40 kmph at isolated places in Kerala between 25 and 27 November. It also forecast rain in Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Mahe over the same period.
Weather experts said intense, localised rain is common in Kerala in the post-monsoon season.

The flooding drew political criticism. State Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala said the municipal corporation, ruled by the BJP, had not made the necessary preparations despite weather warnings of heavy rain. In a Facebook post, he said police clearing garbage was not part of their official duties, but "a humane force cannot stand by and watch people in distress."
CPI(M) leaders V Sivankutty and V K Prasanth criticised the corporation and its mayor, V V Rajesh. They held a protest at the Thampanoor police station. The corporation's response was not available.
keyFacts: East Fort recorded 91 mm of rain in 60 minutes on Thursday.
Light vehicles were diverted; only buses were allowed through flooded stretches.
Water took around two hours to recede after the rain stopped.
IMD forecast winds of 30–40 kmph at isolated places in Kerala from 25 to 27 November.
Friday's yellow alert covers Kottayam, Ernakulam, Idukki, Malappuram, Kozhikode and Wayanad.
stories.background: A yellow alert is the IMD's lowest warning level, asking people to stay aware of the weather. The IMD is the Centre's main weather forecasting agency. Kerala often gets short, intense spells of rain after the monsoon season ends.
stories.whatNext: The IMD's yellow alert for six districts stays in force on Friday, and its thunderstorm forecast runs through 27 November.

stories.headline: SIT names ex-minister B Nagendra a witness, not accused, in Valmiki Corporation case
stories.dek: The Karnataka team's final chargesheet differs from the CBI and ED, which named Nagendra as an accused. Home Minister Priyank Kharge says the decision rests on evidence.
stories.summary: The Karnataka SIT's final chargesheet in the Valmiki Corporation case names former minister B Nagendra as a witness, not an accused. The CBI and ED have named him as an accused; the BJP questions the SIT's independence.
body: The Karnataka Special Investigation Team has named former minister B Nagendra as a witness, not an accused, in its final chargesheet in the Valmiki Corporation case, filed before the Lokayukta special court on November 25.

The case concerns the alleged diversion of about Rs 89.62 crore from the Karnataka Maharshi Valmiki Scheduled Tribes Development Corporation. Nagendra, a Congress MLA from Ballari Rural, has resigned as minister twice over it. The central agencies, which are running their own cases, take a different view of his role.

The 450-page chargesheet also names Basavaraj Daddal, the corporation's former chairman, as a witness. It says Hyderabad-based Satyanarayana Varma induced the then managing director JG Padmanabha, accounts officer Parashuram Durgannanavar and others into transferring more than Rs 90 crore by promising interest or kickbacks. The SIT recovered nearly Rs 80 crore, according to the Times of India's account of the document.

Home Minister Priyank Kharge told reporters in Bengaluru that the SIT acted on evidence. "Clean chit isn't given because I want to. That's not how investigations work," he said. He said no money trail had been found and that about 90 per cent of the transferred money had been recovered.
Kharge said Nagendra had to resign twice because of pressure from the party. Asked whether Nagendra would return to the Cabinet, he said the party high command would decide.

R Ashoka, the BJP's Leader of Opposition in the Assembly, called the outcome "unfortunate". He said there was a suspicion that officials gave the clean chit because of the government's influence. He also said he suspected Nagendra could be made a minister again in the government led by Chief Minister D K Shivakumar.

The Enforcement Directorate filed its prosecution complaint in September 2024, naming Nagendra among 25 accused. It alleged that about Rs 89.6 crore went to 18 fake accounts in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, and that Rs 20.2 crore was distributed in cash during the 2024 general elections.
The CBI's chargesheet, filed in June, named Nagendra among 30 accused. It alleged that he, his associate Nekkanti Nagaraj, Varma and Padmanabha conspired to divert the money.
keyFacts: The SIT's two earlier chargesheets were filed in August 2024.
The ED arrested Nagendra on July 12, 2024; he spent 86 days in jail before bail in October 2024.
The ED named 25 accused and the CBI 30, including Nagendra.
Nagendra resigned a second time on August 28, 2026, weeks after being reinducted.
stories.background: Accounts superintendent Chandrashekar P died at his Shivamogga home on May 26, 2024, leaving a note alleging illegal transfers. Nagendra, then Tribal Development Minister, resigned on June 6, 2024. The ED and CBI began separate cases, and the SIT filed two chargesheets in August 2024. Nagendra was reinducted in August 2026 and resigned again on August 28 after the BJP and JD(S) disrupted the Monsoon session.

stories.headline: 42 US state attorneys general move to block Character.AI sale of user chats
stories.dek: The coalition says the planned auction covers chat histories of more than 21 million US accounts, including over 2.1 million registered to minors, with no safeguards.
stories.summary: A coalition of 42 US state attorneys general is trying to stop Character.AI from selling users' private chat histories during its bankruptcy. They say the data covers more than 21 million US accounts and that buyers face no privacy requirements.
body: A coalition of 42 US state attorneys general is seeking to stop Character.AI from auctioning users' private chat histories as the company goes through Chapter 11 bankruptcy.

Chapter 11 is a US process that lets a company restructure under court supervision, often by selling assets. The attorneys general, the top legal officers of their states, say the data in question covers more than 21 million US accounts. They say more than 2.1 million of those are registered to minors.

In near-identical press releases, the attorneys general said the sale offers "no safeguards for the people whose conversations are being sold." Character.AI is a chatbot service where users talk to customisable AI characters.

The attorneys general list several gaps. They say a buyer would not be required to honour the company's existing privacy policies. Users would have no way to delete their data. Nothing would limit what a buyer does with the data, including selling it on to another party.
They also point to the first bidder, which they say has a limited record. It was established on November 13, 2026, and has no parent company or investors listed.

Character.AI filed for bankruptcy in October after years of legal challenges, including from Disney. Disney bought some of the company's assets and hired its chief executive, Karandeep Anand. A number of the company's technical staff will also join Disney, in a deal known as an acquihire. A similarly broad coalition of attorneys general also opposed that deal.
Separately, New York, Connecticut, California and Colorado have passed laws regulating chatbots. Character.AI may be in violation of them when they take effect on January 1, 2027.
keyFacts: 42 state attorneys general are involved in the effort.
The data covers more than 21 million US accounts.
More than 2.1 million of those accounts are registered to minors.
The first bidder was established on November 13, 2026.
Four states' chatbot laws take effect on January 1, 2027.

stories.headline: COP31 in Antalya ends without an overarching deal, first time since 2009
stories.dek: The European Union and other countries rejected the final proposal from the summit's leadership, which did not name fossil fuels or call for their phase-out.
stories.summary: The COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, ended without an overarching political agreement, the first such outcome since Copenhagen in 2009. Fossil fuels were not named and a proposed adaptation finance target was dropped.
body: The COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, ended without an overarching political agreement, the first time that has happened since the 2009 Copenhagen summit.

The outcome matters in India because the talks covered how fast countries move away from fossil fuels, how much money reaches countries that must adapt to climate change, and a pledge on electricity use that India did not sign.
The European Union and several other countries rejected the final proposal from the summit's Turkish and Australian leadership. The text did not name fossil fuels or call for their phase-out.

The text falls short of the COP28 outcome in Dubai, where countries committed to move away from fossil fuels. Since that meeting, Saudi Arabia, Russia and other oil and gas producers have held back on putting the pledge into practice. Meanwhile, carbon capture, a costly technology that needs a lot of energy, has drawn more attention.

The second point of conflict was adaptation finance, which is money to help vulnerable countries cope with climate impacts. A proposed target of $120 billion a year by 2035 was dropped. It is not clear when or how funds would reach those countries.
Turkey also pushed a goal of raising electricity's share of total energy consumption from 21% to 35% by 2035. Nearly 100 countries signed a separate pledge backing it.
India did not sign. It argued that countries should choose their own energy pathways.

Irish Environment Minister Darragh O'Brien, speaking for EU member states at the closing session, said they were "deeply disappointed" by the result. The talks were scheduled for November 9 to 20 and ran past their end date.
The next conference, COP32, will be held in Ethiopia.
keyFacts: COP31 was held in Antalya, Turkey, and was scheduled to run from November 9 to 20.
A proposed $120 billion a year adaptation finance target for 2035 was dropped.
Nearly 100 countries signed a pledge to lift electricity's share of consumption from 21% to 35% by 2035.
India did not sign the electrification pledge.
COP32 will be held in Ethiopia.
stories.background: At COP28 in Dubai in 2023, countries agreed to transition away from fossil fuels. The last climate summit to end without an overarching political agreement was Copenhagen in 2009. COP31 was led jointly by Turkey and Australia.
stories.whatNext: The next climate conference, COP32, will be held in Ethiopia.

stories.headline: Trump says he asked Putin to pull back military aggression in Europe
stories.dek: Ukraine's President Zelensky said Kyiv has information that Russia is preparing a new mass strike, and told the BBC the US is too focused on the Middle East.
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump said he asked Russian leader Vladimir Putin to pull back military aggression across Europe so a deal on Ukraine could be reached quickly. Zelensky warned of a new Russian mass strike in the coming days.
body: US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that he asked Russian President Vladimir Putin in China to "pull back all Military aggression against territories throughout Europe", in the hope of a quick deal between Russia and Ukraine.
The war has killed people in Ukraine for more than four years, and European governments are watching whether Washington will press Moscow. Trump did not say which territories he meant.
"I really believe this is a strong possibility — Thousands of people are being killed each and every month, A COMPLETE BLOODBATH," Trump wrote on Truth Social.

The post followed a meeting in Florida with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte. In a statement afterwards, Trump said they discussed the importance of Russia and Ukraine avoiding actions that "intentionally, or unintentionally, expand the War". Poland, a NATO member, this week accused Russia of deliberately violating its airspace. Estonia recently linked an arson attack to Russia's military intelligence service.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky gave a different assessment in an interview with the BBC in Kyiv. He said the US was not pushing Russia hard enough in peace talks and that delays in delivering Patriot anti-ballistic missiles were costing lives.

"It's a pity they made a focus on Middle East and they help them more," Zelensky said. He called it "strange" that Trump had described Putin as a friend. "He's an aggressor, and a killer," Zelensky said. The latest talks, mediated in Abu Dhabi earlier this month, made no obvious progress, he said, and are expected to resume in December.

In his nightly video address, Zelensky said Ukraine had information that Russia was preparing a new mass strike. "In the coming days, please pay attention to the alarms of missile threats," he said. It was his second such warning this week.

Russia fired ballistic missiles and 113 drones overnight, Zelensky said, and crews were restoring power in six regions. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said ballistic missiles wounded seven people in the capital and hit a shopping centre and two other buildings. Moscow said it struck drone-related sites in the city.

Ukraine said its drones hit an oil refinery in Russia's Krasnodar region, oil reservoirs at a Transneft facility in Bashkortostan and the Marinovka military airfield in the Volgograd region. Both countries say they do not target civilian sites.
keyFacts: Trump made the request to Putin during talks in China last week.
Zelensky said Ukraine's forces can now destroy about 70% of Russia's fastest drones.
Zelensky said Ukraine has a "very, very big" shortage of ballistic-missile interceptors.
Italy's Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said the sinking of a Russian warship in Libya risked spreading war to the Mediterranean.
stories.background: Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022. Trump has repeatedly urged a negotiated end to the war. He met Putin in China last week and called him "my friend". Talks mediated in Abu Dhabi earlier this month made no obvious progress. Since September, Russia has attacked Kyiv and other cities almost continuously. Ukraine has stepped up long-range strikes on Russian oil sites.
stories.whatNext: Peace talks are expected to resume in December, Zelensky said.

stories.headline: Supreme Court to hear contempt petitions over Thiruparankundram lamp on Friday
stories.dek: Petitioners accuse Madurai officials of not carrying out the court's order, while the temple's hereditary priests say the lamp has never been lit on the hilltop.
stories.summary: The Supreme Court will hear all contempt petitions over the unlit Deepathoon lamp at Thiruparankundram hill on Friday. Hereditary priests say in a letter that the Karthigai Deepam has always been lit near the Uchi Pillaiyar Temple.
body: The Supreme Court will hear all contempt petitions over the Thiruparankundram hill lamp in Madurai on Friday, November 27, after petitioners sought action against the district Collector and other officials.

The case affects devotees, temple authorities and the Tamil Nadu government, which are in dispute over where the Karthigai Deepam, a festival lamp, may be lit on the hill. The court has not yet ruled on whether officials failed to follow its order.
On Thursday, petitioners asked for an early hearing. A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul Pancholi said: "Everything will be listed tomorrow."

On November 20, the bench had allowed a small team authorised by the temple administration to light the lamp at the Deepathoon on November 24, as a one-time measure. The Deepathoon is a stone pillar near the Sikandar Badusha Dargah. The court ordered the Collector to supervise the arrangements and report within three days of the festival.
The lamp was lit on November 24 at the customary Deepa Mandapam near the Uchipillaiyar Temple. The Deepathoon stayed unlit.

In an affidavit on Wednesday, Collector Nishant Krishna apologised to the court. He said he tried to ensure compliance but the temple administration did not allow the lighting, citing established practices and rituals. The state maintains the pillar is only a survey stone put up by the British and has no link to the temple.

At least two contempt petitions have been filed. One, on behalf of original petitioner Rama Ravikumar, concerns non-compliance. Another, by advocate V Ramasubbu, alleges officials deliberately violated the order. One petition seeks to know whether Chief Minister Vijay or any minister instructed officials not to implement it.

The temple trustees resolved on November 24 to keep to the traditional spot, citing Agama rules, which are temple ritual codes. In a letter dated November 25 to the trustees, the hereditary priests said the lamp has always been lit at the Uchi Pillaiyar Temple, directly above the main sanctum. They referred to similar representations of November 7, 2013, and December 4, 2025.
Swaminathan, one of the priests, said: "We have never lit it on the hilltop." He added that lighting it there could be considered if steps with handrails were built.
On Wednesday, Governor Rajendra Arlekar invoked Article 167(b) of the Constitution and sought a report from the state government on why the order was not carried out.
keyFacts: The Supreme Court's November 20 order called the Deepathoon lighting a one-time measure and left the dispute over the site open.
Governor Rajendra Arlekar sought a factual report from the state government on Wednesday under Article 167(b).
The priests' letter is dated November 25; the trustees' resolution is dated November 24.
Madras High Court's Justice GR Swaminathan first ordered lighting at the pillar on December 1, 2025.
stories.background: Devotee Rama Ravikumar went to the Madras High Court after the temple refused to light the lamp at the pillar. On December 1, 2025, a single judge ordered lighting there; the lamp was not lit that year, and a Division Bench upheld the direction on January 6, 2026. The state appealed to the Supreme Court, which on November 20 allowed a one-time lighting and stayed the High Court's findings on the Deepathoon.

stories.headline: Tamil Nadu grants 15 days of paternity leave to married male government staff
stories.dek: The leave can start up to 15 days before a child's birth or be taken within six months after it, according to a government order.
stories.summary: Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay announced 15 days of paternity leave for married male state government employees on Thursday. The government said it is the first such provision in Tamil Nadu and followed requests from employees.
body: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on Thursday announced 15 days of paternity leave for married male state government employees, the first such provision in the state.

The leave applies to fathers who work for the state government. It can begin up to 15 days before the child is born, or be taken within six months of the birth, the government said in an official release.

The government said it acted after male employees asked for a formal paternity leave provision. The order said the father's role in giving physical and emotional support to the mother and in caring for the child is essential.

The order also pointed to the 365 days of maternity leave given to women government employees. It said this reflects the importance given to motherhood and child welfare, and that paternity leave will help men share family responsibilities.

In August, the government announced that women employees having a third child would get 365 days of maternity leave, up from 12 weeks. Tamil Nadu has raised maternity leave in steps: from 90 days to six months in 2011, nine months in 2016 and 365 days in July 2021.

Other states already have similar rules. Odisha introduced 15 days of paternity leave in 2011, and West Bengal gives 30 days of paternity-cum-childcare leave. Kerala provides up to 10 days, Madhya Pradesh 15 days from January 2026, and Assam 14 days since September 2026. Duration and eligibility differ from state to state.

Health Minister K G Arunraj has said the state's Total Fertility Rate has fallen below 1.4, against a replacement level of 2.1. He said nearly 16% of the population is above 60, and that the state might eventually have to consider measures to encourage couples to have more children.
keyFacts: The leave is for married male employees of the Tamil Nadu government.
It can be taken up to 15 days before delivery or within six months of birth.
Maternity leave for women government employees was raised to 365 days in July 2021.
Assam introduced 14 days of paternity leave in September 2026.
stories.background: Vijay, founder of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), has been Tamil Nadu's chief minister since 10 May 2026. His government earlier extended 365 days of maternity leave to women employees having a third child. Health Minister K G Arunraj has said the state's fertility rate is below 1.4.

stories.headline: Sensex and Nifty rise for second day on foreign inflows; rupee slips 24 paise to 92.44
stories.dek: IT shares led gains on Thursday, while the rupee fell on higher crude prices and a US proposal to levy 25 per cent tariffs on Indian goods.
stories.summary: The Sensex gained 390.31 points to close at 84,328.59 on Thursday, led by IT stocks and foreign buying. The rupee weakened 24 paise to 92.44 against the dollar as the RBI's rate decision next week drew attention.
body: The 30-share BSE Sensex rose 390.31 points, or 0.46 per cent, to close at 84,328.59 on Thursday, its second straight gain, helped by foreign fund inflows and buying in IT shares.

The gains matter for investors because both indices have risen sharply this month. The Sensex is up 13.25 per cent in November so far, and the Nifty is up 12.28 per cent. The rupee, meanwhile, lost ground after a strong session on Wednesday.
The 50-share NSE Nifty gained 65.25 points, or 0.25 per cent, to end at 25,884.50. The Sensex touched 84,551.74 during the day.

HCL Tech rose 6.28 per cent, Tata Consultancy Services 4.97 per cent and Infosys 4.70 per cent. Tech Mahindra gained 3.33 per cent. Asian Paints, Bajaj Finance, Bajaj Finserv and Trent were among the laggards. The BSE IT index rose 3.41 per cent.
Foreign institutional investors bought equities worth Rs 4,479.08 crore on Wednesday, according to exchange data.

Vinod Nair, head of research at Geojit Investments, said Indian equities recovered from early losses. He said foreign inflows and selective buying outweighed firm crude and the proposed US tariffs, and that IT tracked a rebound in Asian tech stocks.

Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money, said early gains tapered on uncertainty over the India-US trade agreement and firm US inflation data. He pointed to the possibility of further US Federal Reserve tightening in December.

On Wednesday, the US proposed 25 per cent tariffs on imports from India. The rate would be capped at 17 per cent if the two countries agree a bilateral trade deal. India rejected the US allegations of excess capacity and said it was committed to working with the US for an early trade agreement.

The rupee settled provisionally at 92.44 against the dollar, down 24 paise. It had risen 65 paise to 92.20 on Wednesday. Forex traders said foreign inflows supported the currency, while crude near USD 95 a barrel and tariff fears weighed on it. Brent crude was later down at about USD 93.80.
Rajeev Sharan, head of research at Brickwork Ratings, said the mild reaction suggested the market saw the tariff proposal as an opening position in talks.

The Reserve Bank of India's six-member Monetary Policy Committee meets next week. Market participants expect another repo rate hike. Financial conditions have tightened since the October rate hike, and the banking system was in a liquidity deficit of ₹32,216 crore on Wednesday, according to RBI data.
Madan Sabnavis, chief economist at Bank of Baroda, said he expected open market purchases of government securities. He said the RBI might announce some measures at the policy.
keyFacts: The three-month certificate of deposit rate has risen about 100 basis points since early October to 7.5-7.6 per cent.
The rupee traded between 92.31 and 92.66 on Thursday after opening at 92.50.
The rupee's record closing low is 96.88, set on October 8.
The minimum daily cash reserve ratio requirement for banks was raised from 90 per cent to 99 per cent.
The dollar index stood at 103.70, up 0.09 per cent.
stories.background: The RBI raised its policy rate in October. The rupee hit a record closing low of 96.88 against the dollar on October 8 and has since recovered nearly 5 per cent. The US trade representative's investigation of 16 economic jurisdictions preceded the tariff proposal on India.
stories.whatNext: The RBI's Monetary Policy Committee is scheduled to meet next week, with a repo rate decision expected.

stories.headline: Bangladesh police use tear gas on garment workers protesting wage rise
stories.dek: The protest in Gazipur came a day after a wage board approved a 36% minimum wage rise that workers say is too low.
stories.summary: Bangladesh police used tear gas and stun devices on Thursday against garment workers who tried to shut a main highway. The workers want higher pay after a wage board approved a 36% rise in the minimum wage.
body: Police in Bangladesh used tear gas and sound grenades on Thursday to break up a crowd of garment workers who were trying to shut a main highway over pay.

The garment industry employs more than 4 million people in a country of around 175 million. Bangladesh is the world's second-largest garment exporter after China. Weeks of protests have closed factories, blocked roads, damaged property and slowed production.
Police said protesters set fire to a police motorcycle in Gazipur, one of the country's main garment manufacturing hubs and a centre of the agitation. Police said order had since returned.
"The situation is now calm, but we remain on alert," said Mohammad Amjad Hossain, superintendent of Gazipur Industrial Police.

The protest began a day after a six-member, government-appointed wage board approved a 36% increase in the minimum wage for garment workers. It is the smallest rise in four decades. Workers had called for the sum to be doubled.
The board announced its decision in the early hours of Wednesday, after nearly 12 hours of talks between workers' and employers' representatives. Protests began within hours.

Labour rights advocates said the rise fell well short of workers' demands and would not provide a living wage. Labour rights groups are also urging global fashion brands to pay their suppliers more, so that workers can earn enough to live on.

Separate political tension and violence have also followed former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's plan to return to Dhaka from self-imposed exile in India. Together with the wage protests, this has raised fears of fresh instability in the country.
keyFacts: The wage board has six members and met for nearly 12 hours before deciding.
The 36% rise is the smallest in four decades.
The new minimum wage is 17,000 taka a month.
Police said a police motorcycle was set on fire in Gazipur.
stories.background: Bangladesh's wage board raised the monthly minimum wage for garment workers by 36% to 17,000 taka on Wednesday, after weeks of protests. The industry earns around $38 billion a year and supplies retailers including H&M, Zara, Walmart, Target and Gap. Workers say pay has not kept pace with the cost of food, housing, transport and health care.

stories.headline: X adds parental controls for accounts of 13-to-17-year-olds
stories.dek: Teen accounts will default to a "protected mode", and teenagers will be able to see every restriction a parent applies, the company said.
stories.summary: X has introduced parental controls that let parents manage what teenagers aged 13 to 17 see on the platform. Teen accounts will default to "protected mode", with no sensitive content and no targeted ads.
body: X, the platform that was earlier called Twitter, has introduced parental controls for users aged 13 to 17, the company said.

The tools matter to families because teenagers use the platform even though it is not built for them. X requires users to be at least 13. A 2024 study found that close to a third of children in Generation Alpha, the youngest age group, had an account on X.
Accounts of 13-to-17-year-olds will be set to "protected mode" by default, X said. In this mode they cannot see sensitive content and are not shown targeted ads.

Parents and guardians can see how much time a teenager spends on X each week and set daily limits. They can require approval for new followers and limit feed recommendations and videos to accounts the teenager already follows.
They can also filter specific words, turn off sensitive media, decide who may send their teenager direct messages, and see who the teenager is messaging.
There are limits to what parents can see. They cannot read private messages, view search or viewing history, or post as their teenager.
Teenagers can see which restrictions have been placed on their accounts. Michael O'Herlihy, head of safety at X, wrote in a blog post: "Parents want practical tools, and teens deserve room to grow."
He added that families can set guardrails that fit their home "while teens keep ownership of their accounts and can see every change".
The controls follow criticism of X months ago over a lack of safeguards to stop its AI chatbot being used to generate sexualised images of children and women.
keyFacts: Parental controls apply to accounts of users aged 13 to 17.
Parents can set daily time limits and see weekly time spent on X.
Parents cannot read private messages or see search and viewing history.
Michael O'Herlihy is head of safety at X.
X requires users to be at least 13 years old.
stories.background: X, formerly Twitter, has long required users to be at least 13. It faced criticism months ago over the lack of controls to stop its AI chatbot being used to generate sexualised images of children and women.

stories.headline: India presents Ahmedabad's 2036 Olympic bid to IOC Future Host Commission
stories.dek: The 30-minute online presentation stressed sports infrastructure and anti-doping measures; six other countries are also bidding for the 2036 Games.
stories.summary: India presented its roadmap for hosting the 2036 Olympic and Paralympic Games, with Ahmedabad as the proposed host city, to the IOC's Future Host Commission on Thursday. The IOC will now run an anonymous survey on public views of the bid.
body: India presented Ahmedabad as its proposed host city for the 2036 Olympic and Paralympic Games in an online meeting with the International Olympic Committee's Future Host Commission on Thursday, November 26.

A successful bid would bring the Games to India for the first time. The presentation stressed how quickly sports infrastructure has grown in the country and the anti-doping measures taken over the last couple of years.

The 30-minute presentation was given by outgoing Indian Olympic Association (IOA) President P T Usha and the association's chief executive, Raghuram Iyer. A short discussion followed with the nine-member commission, which is led by Kolinda Grabar-Kitarovic.
Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya attended the meeting at the Sports Authority of India headquarters. He has said repeatedly that doping would be tackled on a war footing.
India has topped the World Anti-Doping Agency's list of violators among major nations for the last three years.

In a press release after the meeting, the IOA said the presentation covered Ahmedabad's preparedness. It said it also covered India's experience in hosting major international sporting events, proposed venue development plans and the long-term vision for delivering the Games.
Germany, Hungary, Qatar, the Republic of Korea, South Africa and Turkiye are the other countries bidding for the 2036 Games.
After the presentation, the IOC will conduct an anonymous survey to gauge the general public's view of India's bid.
keyFacts: The presentation lasted 30 minutes and was held online.
The Future Host Commission has nine members and is led by Kolinda Grabar-Kitarovic.
Six other countries are bidding for the 2036 Games.

stories.headline: Hyderabad police raid hostels over alleged illegal egg-donor network linked to clinics
stories.dek: Police found nearly 40 women from several states in two hostels on October 30; the women's commission says clinics could not explain missing records or how they found donors.
stories.summary: Police raided two Hyderabad women's hostels on October 30 and found nearly 40 women allegedly brought in to sell eggs, which the law bars. The state women's commission says clinics gave evasive answers about how they found donors.
body: Police in Hyderabad raided two women's hostels on October 30 and found nearly 40 women, many allegedly brought from other states to sell their eggs to fertility clinics, an act the law prohibits.
The case concerns women from low-income families who travelled to Telangana for payments of around Rs 50,000 per cycle, and it has put the conduct of fertility clinics under examination.

Police said they acted on a tip-off and searched hostels in Begumpet and Saroornagar at the same time. The women came from West Bengal, Chhattisgarh, Bihar, Assam, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Jharkhand, Delhi and Odisha. Many were Muslim or Dalit, the report said.

At the Begumpet hostel, police found 12 women. Some told police that Nikhat Parvin and Amit Sharma, who ran the hostel, had brought them there with the promise of money for egg donation. The FIR names three clinics where they were told they would undergo procedures: Padmaja, Narmada and Oasis.

Nikhat was arrested on charges of running a racket to sell human gametes, which is banned under the Assisted Reproductive Technology (Regulation) Act. She and Sharma are also charged with human trafficking, cheating, criminal conspiracy and organised crime. They are accused of acting as agents who bring donors to clinics for money.

Begumpet Assistant Commissioner of Police P Gopala Krishna Murthy said the accused found donors through past donors' recommendations and through sub-agents in other states, who identified women in financial difficulty. In some cases, he said, women were allegedly brought with promises of other work and later persuaded to donate.
The Act allows a woman to donate eggs only once in her life, with no more than seven retrieved. It bans selling gametes, running an agency to sell them, and using intermediaries to obtain donors.

The Health Department has found memorandums of understanding allegedly signed between an egg bank called Oasis and facilitators, including Sharma and Nikhat. They provide for payments of up to Rs 65,000 for each cycle of supplying donors.

Nerella Sharada, chairperson of the Telangana State Commission for Women, said many clinics summoned by the body could not explain missing records or how they found donors. "The clinics claim they do not hire any agents or intermediaries to bring donors and that all their donors have turned up at their clinic voluntarily," she said, adding that over 90% of donors appeared to be vulnerable women from distant states.

One woman, identified as Maryam, a Kolkata resident, said she came to Hyderabad on October 10 to pay off a Rs 1 lakh loan and had begun hormone injections before the raid. She spent nearly two weeks in shelter homes and returned home with no earnings. "I didn't know it was illegal," she said.
Authorities have so far found no evidence that clinics deceived couples seeking IVF. Police and health officials are still examining how far women were exploited and what role the clinics played.
keyFacts: Police raided hostels in Begumpet and Saroornagar on October 30.
The FIR names three clinics: Padmaja, Narmada and Oasis.
The law allows one egg donation per woman, with no more than seven oocytes retrieved.
Alleged agreements with Oasis set payments of up to Rs 65,000 per cycle to facilitators.
Nikhat Parvin was arrested; she and Amit Sharma face trafficking and organised crime charges.
stories.background: In July 2025, a separate Hyderabad case involved Universal Srushti Fertility Centre, whose doctor Dr Namratha was accused of running a network that gave a couple another family's baby as their surrogate child. The current case involves egg donation, not surrogacy, and authorities have not found clinics deceiving IVF couples.

stories.headline: Calcutta HC asks police for report on alleged assault of TMC block president
stories.dek: Justice Saugata Bhattacharyya ordered the Bishnupur police station chief to detail the steps taken on Gnanananda Samanta's complaint, and directed protection for him and his family if needed.
stories.summary: The Calcutta High Court on Wednesday ordered police to file a detailed report on the alleged assault and naked parading of Trinamool Congress block president Gnanananda Samanta in Bishnupur. The case returns to court on January 6, 2027.
body: The Calcutta High Court on Wednesday ordered West Bengal police to file a detailed report on allegations that Trinamool Congress block president Gnanananda Samanta was assaulted and paraded naked in Bishnupur.
The case matters because Samanta says police have treated a serious attack as a minor offence. He has asked the court for an independent and effective investigation.

Justice Saugata Bhattacharyya first suggested the matter go to the local magistrate, since the plea mainly concerned an unsatisfactory investigation. He later noted the gravity of the incident. He directed the Inspector-in-Charge of Bishnupur Police Station to report on the steps taken on Samanta's complaint.

In his petition, Samanta said his office-cum-house at Bibighat in Bishnupur was attacked on the night of August 25 by men armed with sticks, stones and sharp objects. He alleged they were working under the directions of the Bharatiya Janata Party. The BJP's response was not given in the court record.
Samanta said the attackers first took his mobile phone, ATM card and government-issued IDs. They then kicked and beat him, he said, and later stripped him, beat him again and paraded him.

He was admitted to a private hospital in Kolkata. His wife then wrote to the police station chief, saying the offences were cognizable, meaning police can act on them without a court order. Samanta said police played down the offences when they registered the FIR, or first information report. A complaint was also registered with the West Bengal Human Rights Commission.

Senior Advocate Soumya Mazumder, for Samanta, said police framed charges only for mischief and criminal intimidation under Section 351 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. "The petitioner (Samanta) was belted around the neck and dragged on the street in front of the police, naked," he told the court.

Justice Bhattacharyya asked what steps police had taken on the FIR. The State's counsel sought time to file a report. The court also directed police to give Samanta and his family protection if the need arises.
The matter will be heard again on January 6, 2027.
keyFacts: The petition is titled Gnanananda Samanta v. State of West Bengal and Ors.
The alleged attack began on the night of August 25 at Bibighat, Bishnupur.
Police charged mischief and criminal intimidation under Section 351 of the BNS, the petitioner's counsel said.
Samanta's complaint was also registered with the West Bengal Human Rights Commission.

stories.whatNext: The High Court will hear the matter again on January 6, 2027.

stories.headline: EU leaders pick Spain's Pablo Hernández de Cos to succeed Lagarde at ECB
stories.dek: The former Bank of Spain governor will be the first Spaniard to lead the European Central Bank, with inflation in the eurozone at 4%.
stories.summary: EU leaders chose Pablo Hernández de Cos on Thursday to be the next European Central Bank president, replacing Christine Lagarde. He takes over in February as eurozone inflation stands at 4%, twice the bank's target.
body: European Union leaders on Thursday chose Spain's Pablo Hernández de Cos, a former Bank of Spain governor, to succeed Christine Lagarde as president of the European Central Bank.

The ECB sets interest rates for the 21 countries that use the euro, which affects borrowing costs, prices and government debt. Inflation in the eurozone reached 4% last month, up from 2.1% a year earlier.

Agreement came at a summit in Brussels. The leaders also agreed two seats on the ECB's executive board: France's Laurence Boone and Germany's Markus Brunnermeier. European Council president António Costa said this "will pave the way for the formal appointment of the new ECB leadership by the EUCO in December".

French President Emmanuel Macron said: "A consensus emerged on the nominations to the European Central Bank." The way was cleared after the Netherlands backed Hernández de Cos, effectively standing down its own candidate, Klaas Knot, the former head of the Dutch central bank.

Hernández de Cos, 55, is general manager of the Bank for International Settlements, which brings together the world's major central banks. He will be the first Spaniard to lead the bank, and the fifth head since its founding in 1998. He is due to take over when Lagarde steps down on February 7, nine months before her term ends. Lagarde announced her early exit less than a month ago.

Analysts described him as a continuity candidate who leans towards easier monetary policy. Matthew Ryan of the financial services firm Ebury said: "We do not expect his appointment to alter the near-term rate path." He noted that the president is one voice on the governing council.

Policymakers appear to agree that a rate rise in December is likely, and markets expect one more increase after that. French public finances will be watched closely. French debt is forecast to reach 122% of GDP next year.

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez welcomed the choice, calling it "a Spain that is leading in Europe as never before". Spain holds a general election on Sunday. The euro rose slightly against the dollar after the news.
The appointment still needs approval from the European Parliament and the ECB's governing council. Both steps are seen as formalities.
keyFacts: Hernández de Cos was chosen over Klaas Knot, former head of the Dutch central bank.
Laurence Boone of France and Markus Brunnermeier of Germany get ECB executive board seats.

stories.background: The ECB, based in Frankfurt, sets monetary policy for the eurozone and aims to keep prices stable. Hernández de Cos was governor of the Bank of Spain from 2018 to 2024 and has chaired the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision. He has headed the Bank for International Settlements since July 2025.
stories.whatNext: European leaders are due to make the formal appointment at the European Council summit in December, after which Parliament and the ECB governing council review it.

stories.headline: US officials split on whether Alice Huang was a Chinese spy, as Vance defends Nvidia CEO
stories.dek: Vice President JD Vance said he has seen no evidence of wrongdoing by Jensen Huang, while the FBI, CIA and Secretary of State Marco Rubio read the same intelligence differently.
stories.summary: US national security officials agree on the facts but not their meaning in the case of Alice Huang, who had contact with China's spy agency, according to Reuters-sourced accounts. Vice President JD Vance said Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is not under federal investigation.
body: US national security agencies and the White House remain divided over whether Alice Huang, a former executive at a major Nvidia customer, worked for China's Ministry of State Security, five people familiar with the matter told Reuters.

The question matters because it sits behind President Donald Trump's push to bring back Jensen Huang as chief executive of Nvidia, the chipmaker whose processors power much of the world's artificial intelligence (AI) work. Members of both parties in Congress have vowed to investigate national security risks and conflict-of-interest concerns.

The five people, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the FBI, the CIA and Rubio, who is national security adviser and secretary of state, agree on the underlying facts. They differ on what those facts mean. The people said the differing views were not formally debated inside the administration before Huang was ousted from Nvidia earlier this month.

Two of the people said US agencies have collected intelligence on Alice Huang's contact with people linked to the Ministry of State Security, the MSS, which is China's civilian spy agency. They said the FBI has told recent briefings that the intelligence does not show she is an officer or an asset of Chinese intelligence.

The CIA's view is more nuanced, the two people said. It holds that the reporting does not clearly show she had sensitive national security information or passed it to China, but it has not ruled out new evidence. Its analysis says she was in touch with the agency partly because Chinese law requires citizens to cooperate with intelligence authorities. Some other officials see the contact itself as a sign of cooperation with Beijing.

Vance, speaking to reporters on Wednesday in Ohio, said the administration had been told Huang was under no investigation. "I just don't think that people should lose their jobs because anonymous sources accuse them of things in the New York Times when those things actually aren't rooted in real evidence," he said. He cited conversations with the Justice Department and other national security officials.

Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton said it was unclear whether Alice Huang was an asset of Chinese intelligence services. Attorney General Todd Blanche told journalists on Tuesday: "I have no reason to stand up here and say Nvidia is anything but a good corporate citizen." Rubio has not spoken publicly about Nvidia since Huang returned, and one person said he was caught off guard by the reinstatement.

China has denied the espionage allegations and has called them a smear. Megaspeed, where Alice Huang worked until August 2025, says its business is lawful and that it complies with US export controls. Jensen Huang has acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife and apologised, but has not addressed the allegations in detail. The White House, CIA, FBI and State Department declined to comment to Reuters.

One person said CIA reporting focused mainly on Alice Huang's role at Megaspeed and its diversion of US chips to China. Many officials consider that a bigger national security threat than the affair, the people said. The intelligence reports were not shared with Congress, they said.
keyFacts: Five people familiar with the matter described the split; none was named.
The FBI's recent briefings say the intelligence does not show Alice Huang is an MSS officer or asset.
Vance spoke on Wednesday after serving Thanksgiving lunch at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base in Ohio.
Alice Huang, a Chinese national, worked at Megaspeed, which says it complies with US export controls.
Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang on Monday.
stories.background: Nvidia's board ousted Jensen Huang on November 12 after he acknowledged an affair with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive. A classified memo overseen by Rubio had raised concerns that she had links to Chinese intelligence; the New York Times reported on it. Trump lobbied the board, which reinstated Huang on Monday. Nvidia shares recovered after falling more than 10%. US agencies are investigating Megaspeed over suspected chip diversion to China.

stories.headline: Nvidia pauses server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries
stories.dek: The halt follows a new US Commerce Department rule requiring licences for buyers of advanced AI chips in the region, where Chinese firms have rented computing power.
stories.summary: Nvidia has told manufacturing partners to stop shipping servers to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia. The pause follows new US export rules meant to stop Chinese companies reaching advanced AI chips through data centres in the region.
body: Nvidia has told manufacturing partners, including Dell and Super Micro, to pause server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia, as the US tightens rules meant to keep advanced AI chips from China.

The four countries host data centres that Chinese companies have used to get at Nvidia's chips. Servers are the machines that hold the chips and run AI models. A halt can delay data centre projects and the AI services built on them.

The partners package Nvidia's chips into servers. They have told buyers in the four countries that Nvidia will not allow their orders to ship, according to three people with knowledge of the matter. It is not clear whether the halt is temporary. Nvidia and its partners are trying to work out how to comply with the new rules, those people said. Nvidia declined to comment. Dell, Supermicro, ByteDance and Aolani did not respond to requests for comment.

Many Chinese groups have rented access to Nvidia chips through cloud computing providers, which buy servers containing them. The US Commerce Department issued new rules last week aimed at ending that practice. The rule adds licence requirements for five countries, including Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand, and limits chip sales to non-US data centres that supply large amounts of computing power to Chinese-headquartered firms.
The Institute for Progress, a think tank, estimates that remote data centres like these supply about 24% of China's AI computing power.

The Commerce Department has given cloud providers 90 days to obtain a licence by showing that their end users do not include restricted entities. An executive at a cloud provider said: "There's this new rule but no guidance on execution. No one knows how to apply for this licence while the 90-day clock is ticking."

The region is important to Nvidia's sales. Company accounts show US$104 billion in revenue was routed through its Singapore subsidiary in 2025, up 72 per cent in a year. Some revenue earned in Taiwan and China is also recorded by that unit.

Aolani, a Singapore-based cloud company, had planned to provide computing power to ByteDance, the Chinese owner of TikTok, through leasing agreements, said two of the people. Some bankers who had agreed to finance the project have stopped issuing credit worth about $500mn, and ByteDance may drop the deal, they said.
Chief executive Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia's top job this week after being briefly ousted. The people said there is little sign that the company will hold back from applying the new rules.
keyFacts: Dell and Super Micro are among the partners told to pause server shipments.
Cloud providers have 90 days to obtain licences under the Commerce Department rule.

stories.background: The US first restricted advanced chip exports to China in October 2022 and has tightened the rules since. A global licence rule issued in January 2025 was not enforced by the Trump administration, and it was formally replaced only last week. Until then, firms in countries such as Singapore could buy advanced chips for data centres without a licence. Megaspeed has been investigated for over two years over whether it diverted chips to China, and has denied wrongdoing.
stories.whatNext: Cloud providers have 90 days from the Commerce Department's rule to obtain licences, and it is not yet clear when Nvidia's pause will end.

stories.headline: Thanksgiving storm floods US East Coast, cuts power to over 836,000 customers
stories.dek: Gusts of up to 72 mph, coastal flooding and more than 400 flight cancellations hit travel on Thursday, and New York postponed its Macy's parade to Saturday.
stories.summary: A storm brought gusts of up to 70 mph and coastal flooding to the US East Coast on Thursday. More than 836,000 utility customers lost power, flights were cancelled, and two states declared emergencies.
body: A powerful storm swept up the US East Coast on Thursday, Thanksgiving Day, cutting power to more than 836,000 utility customers and flooding low-lying coastal areas, according to poweroutage.us.
The holiday is one of the busiest travel periods in the US. Flights were delayed or cancelled, roads were closed, and New York postponed its Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade.

Gusts reached 70 mph (112 kph), bringing down trees and power lines. AccuWeather meteorologist Alyssa Glenny said gusts had reached 72 mph at Stingray Point, Virginia. Coastal New Jersey and Long Island were bracing for gusts of up to 80 mph. New York City Emergency Management reported winds of 56 mph (90 kph) at LaGuardia Airport.

The largest outages were in Virginia (more than 174,000), Maryland (172,000) and Pennsylvania (almost 170,000). Missouri had more than 117,000, New Jersey over 91,000, Delaware over 20,000 and North Carolina nearly 16,000.

The National Weather Service said strong onshore winds and king tides, the seasonal high tides, were flooding low-lying communities. It issued coastal flood warnings for counties in New York and New Jersey, including all five boroughs of New York City.

In Avalon, New Jersey, local official Scott J Wahl said the town saw some of its worst flooding in its history. Several drivers had to be rescued after driving around barricades into flood water. Atlantic City's mayor, Marty Small Sr, urged residents of flood-prone areas to leave voluntarily. "This is more like a tropical storm than a nor'easter," he said.

In Virginia, the Chesapeake Bay Bridge-Tunnel closed for several hours because of wind. In North Carolina, the only highway linking Hatteras Island to the mainland was closed after seawater breached the dunes and covered the road.

FlightAware reported more than 2,200 US-related delays and more than 400 cancellations on Thursday. Baltimore/Washington International and New York's John F. Kennedy airports were among the worst affected. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy urged travellers to stay in touch with their airlines.

Governor Mikie Sherrill declared a state of emergency across New Jersey. Governor Kathy Hochul declared one for parts of New York. Wind advisories ran from northern Georgia through the mid-Atlantic into southern New England.
Macy's moved its 100th parade to Saturday, saying safety was its top priority. It is the first time the parade has been postponed. The new start time is 8:30 a.m. in New York.

Elsewhere, heavy snow fell in Missouri and Illinois. St Louis recorded 7.3 inches (18.5 centimetres) and Ste. Genevieve, Missouri, 14 inches. On the West Coast, record tides forced evacuations in parts of California.

The weather service said conditions would improve across the Mid-Atlantic overnight as the heaviest rain and wind moved into New England. Gusts of 25-35 mph were still expected in parts of the East Coast on Friday. Glenny said New York City should be dry on Saturday.
keyFacts: Poweroutage.us counted more than 836,000 customers without power at 4:06 p.m. ET on Thursday.

Los Angeles and Santa Barbara tied or broke all-time high tide records on Wednesday, the weather service said.
stories.background: King tides are seasonal high tides. This year they overlapped with other factors that raised their impact, including unusually high Pacific coast water levels. Forecasters had warned earlier in the week that the East Coast storm could ground the parade's giant balloons.
stories.whatNext: The Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade is due to start at 8:30 a.m. in New York on Saturday.
