stories.headline: Gérard Depardieu ordered to stand trial for rape after appeal fails
stories.dek: The Paris Court of Appeal dismissed a second allegation of rape, which related to an incident six days later, so the trial will cover one alleged rape.
stories.summary: A Paris appeals court on Thursday rejected Gérard Depardieu's challenge and ordered the 77-year-old actor to stand trial for the alleged rape of actress Charlotte Arnould in 2018. He denies the allegation, and his lawyers are weighing a further appeal.
body: The Paris Court of Appeal on Thursday upheld an order for French actor Gérard Depardieu, 77, to stand trial for the alleged rape of actress Charlotte Arnould at his Paris home in 2018.
Depardieu is one of the best-known names in French cinema. The case follows his decision, less than two weeks ago, to drop an appeal against a separate sexual assault conviction.

Arnould was 22 at the time. She reported the allegations to police a few days after she went to his home to rehearse a play. She has waived her right to anonymity. Depardieu has denied the allegation. In a letter published in Le Figaro in 2023, he wrote: "there was never any coercion or violence between us."
The court ruled that he should be tried over what happened on August 7, 2018. It dismissed the allegation of a second rape six days later, at a hotel.
An investigating judge had sent Depardieu to trial in August 2025. He challenged that decision. If the trial goes ahead, he could face up to 20 years in prison.
Arnould's lawyer, Carine Durrieu Diebolt, spoke outside the court. She said the ruling was "genuinely a relief" and a victory for her client.

Depardieu's lawyer Delphine Meillet told The Associated Press that he disputes the decision. She did not say whether he would appeal further. Another lawyer, David-Olivier Kaminski, said the court had partly ruled in his favour and that the team would look into an appeal to the Court of Cassation, France's highest court for civil and criminal cases.
Arnould's case was first dismissed for lack of evidence. After she filed a civil complaint, a judicial investigation opened in the summer of 2020.

In May 2025, Depardieu was convicted of sexually assaulting two women on the set of the film Les Volets Verts. He received an 18-month suspended prison sentence. On November 16, he said he accepted the sentence and offered "deep and sincere apologies" to those who may have suffered.
French authorities have also confirmed a separate inquiry involving Depardieu and author Michel Houellebecq over allegations of a sexual nature linked to the 2018 film Thalasso.

His conduct towards women drew fresh scrutiny after a 2023 television documentary showed him making obscene remarks during a 2018 trip to North Korea.

stories.dek: Fast bowler Brar replaces Prasidh Krishna as India make one change from the drawn Wellington Test; New Zealand name an unchanged XI.
stories.summary: India captain Shubman Gill won the toss and chose to field in the second and final Test at Hagley Oval, Christchurch. Gurnoor Brar made his debut in place of Prasidh Krishna.
body: India captain Shubman Gill won the toss and chose to bowl first against New Zealand in the second and final Test at Hagley Oval in Christchurch on Friday.

India need a win to take the series and to keep alive their hopes of reaching the World Test Championship final. The first Test in Wellington was drawn. A win would also give India their first Test series victory in New Zealand since 2009.
India made one change to the XI that played in Wellington. Fast bowler Gurnoor Brar received his Test cap from Jasprit Bumrah and came in for Prasidh Krishna. Mohammed Siraj was not in the side.
New Zealand, led by Tom Latham, named the same XI as in Wellington. That keeps fast bowler Jacob Duffy in the team.

The pitch carries a thick covering of grass, and the ball is expected to seam and move early. Teams fielding first have won nine of the 15 Tests at Hagley Oval, and fast bowlers have taken 90% of the wickets at the ground. The curator has said the surface should ease for batting from the third day.
Drizzle had fallen in Christchurch since Wednesday evening, and both teams trained indoors. AccuWeather forecast sunny conditions for the first two days, with a chance of rain on Monday and Tuesday.

stories.headline: Gukesh and Sindarov draw Game 3 of World Championship after 60 moves
stories.dek: Sindarov made his 40th move with six seconds left on his clock as the match stayed level at 1.5-1.5 going into the first rest day.
stories.summary: D Gukesh and Javokhir Sindarov drew the third game of the World Chess Championship in Geneva on Thursday after 60 moves. The match is level at 1.5-1.5, with Game 4 on Saturday.
body: Defending champion D Gukesh and challenger Javokhir Sindarov of Uzbekistan drew Game 3 of the World Chess Championship in Geneva on Thursday, ending a 60-move game on a repetition of moves.
The result keeps the 14-game match level at 1.5-1.5. All three games so far have been drawn, and the players now have Friday off as the first rest day. Gukesh plays white in Game 4 on Saturday.

The Guardian reported that the game lasted 4 hours 49 minutes, the longest of the match so far. Sindarov had white and opened with the Ruy Lopez. Gukesh answered with the Berlin Defence, which he also used in Game 1, but he changed course with a bishop move on the fifth turn.

Gukesh played his first 13 moves in about two minutes, which suggested he had prepared the line. Sindarov used far more time. By the 11th turn he had spent 30 minutes more than Gukesh, and at one stage he was nearly 50 minutes behind on the clock.

The queens came off the board on the 16th turn. By the 23rd turn the game had reached an ending with two rooks each and bishops on opposite-coloured squares. Gukesh still had more than half an hour extra and chose to press, though the position pointed towards a draw.
A bishop move by Gukesh on the 27th turn put him under some pressure, and Sindarov tried to take advantage. Gukesh defended accurately and posed some threats of his own.

Sindarov then ran short of time. He made his 40th move, the first time control, with six seconds left. That move gave both players an extra 30 minutes. The game ended in a draw by repetition on the 60th turn.
Game 1 ended in a draw after 38 moves and Game 2 after 20 moves, by threefold repetition.

stories.headline: Delhi's air stays 'poor' for 12th day as chest clinics are set up
stories.dek: The India Meteorological Department forecast that air quality will worsen to 'very poor' from November 28-29, with ventilation expected to be weak.
stories.summary: Delhi's AQI settled at 224 on Thursday, the 12th straight day in the 'poor' category. Secondary organic aerosols were the largest source of PM2.5, and the government has told district hospitals to open chest clinics.
body: Delhi's air quality stayed in the "poor" category on Thursday for the 12th day in a row, with the Air Quality Index at 224.

The city's residents are breathing this air as the forecast points to a worsening. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) said the air is likely to turn "very poor" from November 28-29. Hospitals have been told to prepare for patients with pollution-related illness.

Of the 55 monitoring stations that reported data, 40 were in the "poor" category and 14 in the "moderate" category. One, the ITO station, recorded "very poor" air. The AQI was 227 on November 24 and 220 on November 25.
The Central Pollution Control Board rates an AQI of 201 to 300 as "poor" and 301 to 400 as "very poor".

Real-time source estimates for Thursday showed secondary organic aerosols as the largest contributor to PM2.5, at 24.8 per cent. These are fine particles that form in the air when gases from vehicles, industry and other burning react with other compounds.

Vehicles contributed 20.6 per cent, biomass burning 19.7 per cent and secondary inorganic pollutants 12.5 per cent. Waste burning accounted for 11.4 per cent and road dust, soil and minerals for 4.5 per cent. Firecrackers contributed 1.4 per cent.
The IMD's early warning system said air quality would stay "poor" on November 26 and 27. For the six days after that, it forecast "very poor" to "poor" air.

The IMD forecast the maximum mixing depth, the height up to which pollutants can spread, at 1,050 metres on November 27 and 28. A lower depth keeps pollutants closer to the ground. The ventilation index was forecast at 1,200 square metres per second on November 27 and 1,300 on November 28. The IMD said a value below 6,000, together with wind slower than 10 kilometres per hour, is unfavourable for dispersing pollutants.

In August, the Union health ministry directed district hospitals and medical colleges to set up chest clinics to run from September to February. The National Centre for Disease Control issued guidelines requiring staff to examine and treat patients and to counsel them on avoiding pollution-related illness.

On November 6, the Delhi health department told district hospitals to open the clinics within a week. Newslaundry visited hospitals in Burari, Jahangirpuri and GTB Nagar. In Burari, a resident named Geeta said she has had a cough, chest pain and breathing difficulty since Diwali.
The IMD forecast puts "very poor" air in Delhi from November 28.

stories.headline: Mediation in Sunjay Kapur family trust dispute fails; Supreme Court to hear case
stories.dek: Rani Kapur's counsel put her claim at ₹6,000 crore, while the trust's assets were valued at around ₹30,000 crore by the opposing side's counsel.
stories.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday closed mediation led by former Chief Justice DY Chandrachud between Rani Kapur and Priya Kapur over the RK Family Trust. The court said the parties must now argue the case, and asked the Delhi High Court to decide a pending interim plea in a time-bound manner.
body: Mediation led by former Chief Justice of India DY Chandrachud between Rani Kapur and her daughter-in-law Priya Sachdev Kapur failed, the Supreme Court was told on Thursday, after 15 sittings.

The dispute is over the RK Family Trust, which holds wealth linked to the Sona Group. It affects Sunjay Kapur's mother, his wife and his children from his marriage to actor Karisma Kapoor. Kapur, former chairman of Sona Comstar, died in June 2025.

A bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran noted from the mediator's report that talks on two issues remained open. One was how Kapur's children with Karisma Kapoor would exit the trust structure. The other was Rani Kapur's claims. The mediator was hopeful on the first, but said the second had reached an impasse.

Senior advocate Siddhartha Dave, for Rani Kapur, said she had sought ₹6,000 crore to settle her claims and had received no counter-proposal in six months. Rani Kapur is 81. Dave said meeting her daughter-in-law caused her considerable anxiety and that she was willing to meet the mediator separately.

Senior advocate Mukul Rohatgi, for Priya Kapur, said Rani Kapur was unwilling to join a joint session. "She walked out after one meeting; and now she is blaming the daughter-in-law. Is this fair?" he said. He told the court the two sides had had enough of mediation.

The court asked who would liquidate assets to pay ₹6,000 crore. It also asked Rohatgi whether, in his client's view, Rani Kapur was entitled to anything. "No," he replied. Dave said that was why mediation had not worked.

Senior advocate Abhimanyu Bhandari, also for Priya Kapur, said she was entitled to 60 per cent of the trust and the remaining 40 per cent should be divided among Sunjay Kapur's children. He said the trust was multi-generational and could not be broken up. Senior advocate Mahesh Jethmalani, for Karisma Kapoor's children, said they were entitled to 24 to 26 per cent.

"One can never force a settlement," the court said. It indicated that the Delhi High Court should decide, in a time-bound manner, the pending application to preserve the trust's assets, and said it would pass a short order. Rani Kapur has challenged the trust's validity, alleging her assets were transferred into it without her informed consent. Her claim is disputed by the other side.
Dave asked for quick hearing of the interim relief sought in the High Court. "The battle begins now," the court replied. "Yes, no doubt," Dave said.
keyFacts: The Supreme Court appointed Chandrachud as mediator on May 7, 2026, with the consent of all parties.
The mediation held 15 sittings before it was closed.
Bhandari said Priya Kapur is entitled to 60 per cent of the trust; Jethmalani said Karisma Kapoor's children are entitled to 24 to 26 per cent.
Sunjay Kapur died in June 2025 while playing polo in England.
stories.background: Rani Kapur moved the Delhi High Court challenging the RK Family Trust, saying her assets were transferred into it without her informed consent. The Supreme Court first suggested mediation on April 27, 2026, and appointed Chandrachud on May 7. In August it was told that six rounds of talks had been held and extended the process.

stories.headline: Shivakumar tells striking ASHA workers no government can be blackmailed
stories.dek: The Karnataka chief minister ruled out a written assurance on the ₹15,000 honorarium demand and said the issue would be discussed in Cabinet and the Assembly session.
stories.summary: Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar said on Thursday that no government can be blackmailed, as the ASHA workers' stir in Bengaluru entered its 10th day. He appealed to them to return to work and refused to give a written assurance.
body: Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar said on Thursday that ASHA workers cannot blackmail the government, and he appealed to them to end their indefinite protest in Bengaluru and return to work.

The workers, who are community health workers appointed under a Centre-run programme, have stayed at Freedom Park day and night since November 17. The Karnataka State Joint ASHA Workers' Association is demanding a monthly honorarium of Rs 15,000 and other pending benefits. Health services in villages and towns rely on them.

Speaking to reporters in Mysuru, Shivakumar said: "You can't blackmail any government, whether it is mine or any other." He added that he was making a humble appeal to them to go back, and that the government would call them for talks.

The workers have asked for a written assurance. Shivakumar refused. "This is not an agreement," he said, adding that such a step would become a practice across the state. He said he could do nothing for those who did not trust the chief minister's word.

He asked why the workers were not seeking a written reply from the Centre, which recruited them and, he said, has not raised its contribution. He said Karnataka was bearing a substantial part of the cost. He also said the demand was not unjust and that the government had raised the honorarium once and would do so again.

Shivakumar said the issue involved serious financial implications because workers in 17 departments have made similar pay demands. He said five to six rounds of discussions had been held and that the matter would go to the Cabinet and the Assembly session in Belagavi. He said the government had made four of the five guarantee schemes available to ASHA workers, all except the one for unemployed youth.

Health Minister U T Khader had said earlier on Thursday that health services were running despite the workers' absence, and that the government might not cooperate if they did not trust its assurances. Khader said the state already pays an additional Rs 5,000 on top of the Centre's amount, and that the demand covers about 41,000 workers.
Asked about this, Shivakumar said the minister's statement had been misinterpreted. "We need everyone. We need all of them," he said.

stories.headline: Kerala weighs action against ex-CPI(M) MLA over speech after Dhanaraj verdict
stories.dek: Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala has told police to examine T I Madhusoodanan's remarks on the court, the acquitted RSS workers and social media critics.
stories.summary: The Kerala government is considering legal action against former Payyannur MLA T I Madhusoodanan over a speech attacking the Dhanaraj murder verdict. Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala has asked police to examine the full speech.
body: The Kerala government is considering legal action against former CPI(M) MLA T I Madhusoodanan over a speech criticising the court verdict in the C V Dhanaraj murder case, Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala said on Thursday.

The speech touches on the safety of people acquitted in a political murder case and on the independence of courts. Chennithala said police were collecting the complete speech and intelligence inputs before deciding what to do.
He said threats by political leaders and former legislators were unacceptable. He urged the CPI(M) leadership to step in to prevent violence and keep the peace.

Health Minister K Muraleedharan also condemned the remarks. He said threats of violence and attacks on judges would not be tolerated, and that parties must respect verdicts even when they disagree. He cited the Congress-UDF's response to the Ariyil Shukoor murder case verdict as an example.

Madhusoodanan, a CPI(M) Kannur district secretariat member, spoke on Wednesday night at a DYFI-organised commemoration in Payyannur. He said the party would settle scores and told the acquitted RSS workers to remember past confrontations.

“If we have to settle scores, we will settle scores. This movement has no hesitation in that,” he said. He also said the judiciary, “as part of the government establishment”, was implementing a policy of crushing Left politics.

He warned critics on social media. “When you people step out onto the streets, we will draw certain boundaries, stop you and ask questions,” he said. He also said he was not saying this to encourage violence.

The Taliparamba Additional Sessions Court gave three RSS workers life sentences for the 2016 killing of Dhanaraj, a CPI(M) activist. It acquitted 16 others, finding the prosecution had not proved their involvement or the conspiracy charge.

The judge criticised the police investigation, saying police were driven by the statement of the first witness, P P Prajeesh, and ignored vital points. Madhusoodanan said the court had refused to accept Prajeesh's evidence because he was a CPI(M) worker. The judgment examined inconsistencies in his account over 17 paragraphs.

Madhusoodanan also thanked the court for rejecting a defence suggestion that he was involved in the murder. Special Public Prosecutor C K Sreedharan has said an appeal will be filed in the High Court against the 16 acquittals.

stories.headline: Gadkari announces ₹1 lakh crore road projects for Bengal, including Kolkata ring road
stories.dek: The Union minister said funds would not be a constraint, and asked the state to prepare detailed plans for multi-tier flyovers and metro corridors in Kolkata.
stories.summary: Union Road Transport Minister Nitin Gadkari announced road projects worth ₹1 lakh crore for West Bengal at Kolaghat on Thursday. They include a 250-km, ₹14,000-crore ring road around Kolkata to ease traffic congestion.
body: Union Road Transport and Highways Minister Nitin Gadkari on Thursday announced road projects worth ₹1 lakh crore for West Bengal, including a 250-km ring road around Kolkata costing an estimated ₹14,000 crore.

The ring road is meant to ease traffic in a city where congestion is a daily problem. Gadkari said the plan followed an appeal from Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari and his ministers. He spoke at an event of the National Highways Authority of India at Kolaghat in Purba Medinipur district.

"I am announcing the approval of a 250-km ring road for Kolkata at a cost of Rs 14,000 crore," Gadkari said. The road is to link Howrah, North and South 24-Parganas, and join the Kona, Belghoria and Kalyani Expressways.

Gadkari said money would not be a constraint. "Do not worry about money. You will get tired of asking for projects, but I will not get tired of providing funds," he told Adhikari. He said the state would develop quickly under what he called a "double-engine government", with Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the Centre.
He asked the state to prepare a detailed project report (DPR) for multi-tier, single-pillar flyovers and metro corridors of the kind built in Nagpur and Pune. He called the announcement a "teaser".

Other projects named include an 8-lane Dankuni–Kolaghat highway at ₹20,000 crore and the Varanasi–Kolkata Greenfield Expressway. Gadkari said the expressway's DPR has gone to the Cabinet. The 820-km corridor has a 235-km stretch in Bengal costing ₹30,000 crore, and would cut travel time between the two cities from 12 hours to five.

The list also includes the Siliguri–Guwahati corridor at ₹26,000 crore, the Gorakhpur–Siliguri Expressway at ₹38,000 crore, and the Siliguri–Darjeeling corridor at ₹6,000 crore. Gadkari also promised road links to Gangasagar.

At the event he inaugurated and laid foundation stones for 22 national highway projects worth ₹8,700 crore. He said highway works worth about ₹40,000 crore had been completed in Bengal, and works worth ₹35,000 crore covering about 450 km were under way.

Speaking to reporters after meeting Gadkari, Adhikari said Bengal lags behind several states in national highways. He said he would seek Modi's help to bring more state roads under the national highway network.

Adhikari said Gadkari had assured support, including around 10,000 electric vehicles for the state. He also said Bengal had been denied its due share of highway investment over the past 15 years because the previous state government and the Centre did not coordinate. Adhikari said the state was set to receive Centre-funded projects worth ₹25,000 crore.
keyFacts: The Kolkata ring road is to be 250 km long and cost an estimated ₹14,000 crore.
Gadkari inaugurated or laid foundation stones for 22 national highway projects worth ₹8,700 crore.
The Varanasi–Kolkata expressway would cut travel time from 12 hours to five, Gadkari said.
Adhikari said Gadkari assured support including around 10,000 electric vehicles for the state.
stories.background: Suvendu Adhikari leads a newly formed BJP government in West Bengal. Nitin Gadkari, a senior BJP leader, has been Union Road Transport and Highways Minister since 2014. The state and the Centre are now run by the same party, which Gadkari called a "double-engine government".
stories.whatNext: Gadkari asked the state to prepare detailed project reports for Kolkata flyovers and metro corridors; the Varanasi–Kolkata expressway report is with the Cabinet.

stories.headline: CBI FIR says NHB audit found funds siphoned via fictitious loans in ₹80-crore case
stories.dek: The agency's FIR against Star Housing Finance cites a forensic audit by the National Housing Bank that describes phantom loan accounts with no files or KYC documents.
stories.summary: The CBI searched six premises linked to Star Housing Finance Ltd and its directors in an alleged ₹80.15-crore fraud on the National Housing Bank. Its FIR cites an NHB forensic audit that describes phantom loan accounts and false repayment entries.
body: The Central Bureau of Investigation has searched six premises linked to Mumbai-based Star Housing Finance Ltd and its directors in an alleged ₹80.15-crore fraud on the National Housing Bank, the agency said.

The National Housing Bank (NHB) is the apex financial institution for housing finance. It lends to housing finance companies and banks against pools of individual home loans, so a loss at this level concerns public-sector money.

The CBI registered its FIR on Monday after a complaint from the NHB against the company, its directors and unidentified public servants. The FIR invokes provisions of the Indian Penal Code and the Prevention of Corruption Act on conspiracy, cheating, breach of trust, falsified accounts and misconduct by public servants.

The complaint covers transactions between the company and the NHB from 2020 to 2025. The NHB alleges the company diverted loan proceeds by disbursing fictitious loans, causing it a wrongful loss of ₹80.15 crore. It classified the account as fraud in July 2026 and reported it to the Reserve Bank of India.

The FIR cites an NHB forensic audit. It says the main method was the creation of phantom loan accounts in the company's loan management system, with no files, dockets or KYC (know-your-customer) documents behind them. The audit said the money was mainly used for share manipulation of the company.

The FIR says these accounts were closed by opening new fictitious accounts using fake KYC documents or employees' names, or by entering false EMI collections. It quotes the audit: "Findings indicated that the false bank book entries and payments recorded without actual bank debits were a manipulation in books."

Those named as accused, besides the company, are promoter A Jain, director K Jain, managing director AK Sachidanand and guarantor NK Jain. These are allegations, and no court has ruled on them. Company officials could not be reached for comment.

The searches took place in Mumbai, Delhi and Udaipur, and the CBI said documents and other records were recovered. The agency is examining the seized material and tracing the movement of the loan funds to establish the roles of the accused.
keyFacts: The alleged loss to the National Housing Bank is ₹80.15 crore.
The transactions under investigation date from 2020 to 2025.
The NHB classified the account as fraud in July 2026.
The CBI registered the FIR on Monday.
Six premises were searched in Mumbai, Delhi and Udaipur.
stories.background: The National Housing Bank was set up by an Act of Parliament in 1987. It supports housing finance firms through refinance, which is funding lent against pools of individual housing loans.

stories.headline: New Zealand's ruling coalition ends one seat short of majority in final results
stories.dek: The National-led bloc now needs the centrist Opportunity Party to govern, or the country may face another election.
stories.summary: Final results show New Zealand's National-led coalition holds 65 of 130 seats, one short of a majority. It needs the Opportunity Party, which has seven seats, or a successful recount, to stay in power.
body: New Zealand's governing coalition, led by Prime Minister Christopher Luxon, fell one seat short of a majority in final election results released on Friday.

The result decides who runs the country. Without a deal with a smaller party, New Zealand may have to vote again. The election was held on November 7, after a campaign dominated by a weak economy and voter frustration over living costs and unemployment.
Luxon's National Party won 40 of the 130 seats. Its partners ACT and New Zealand First won 13 and 12. That gives the bloc 65 seats. A majority needs 66.

Preliminary results on election day had given the bloc a slim two-seat lead. It lost two seats after the electoral commission counted nearly 485,000 special votes, which are cast from overseas or outside a voter's home electorate. Such votes have usually favoured the left.
Labour finished with 36 seats, the Greens 17 and Te Pāti Māori five. A Labour-led government is not possible, even with the support of Opportunity, which won seven seats.

Opportunity is a new centrist party led by Auckland businesswoman Qiulae Wong. She has said the party will negotiate first with the party that wins the most seats. The party has set five bottom-line issues, including action on the supermarket duopoly, a cap on political donations and an end to bottom trawling in fishing.
Luxon had earlier ruled out working with Opportunity. After the election he softened that position and said he intended to find common ground with the party.
A possible obstacle is New Zealand First. Opportunity has said it will not strike a deal if its leader, Winston Peters, serves as foreign affairs minister. Peters has held that post three times.
Three electorate seats changed hands on special votes. Labour won Wairarapa from National by 81 votes and Hamilton East by 173 votes. The Greens won Wellington Bays from Labour by 1,610 votes.

If National asks for a recount and wins back one of those seats, it could reach a majority without Opportunity. Recount applications must be filed by December 3, and results could take another five days.
keyFacts: Opportunity won seven seats in the 130-seat parliament.
Labour won Wairarapa from National by 81 votes.
Special votes counted on Friday numbered nearly 485,000.
In 2023, coalition talks in New Zealand took five weeks.
Opportunity's five demands include capping political donations and a 10-year cross-party health plan.
stories.background: New Zealand uses a proportional system, so parties usually form coalitions. National, ACT and New Zealand First governed together after the 2023 election. A four-party arrangement with Opportunity would be a first for the country.
stories.whatNext: National can apply for a recount of the three seats by December 3, with results possible about five days later.

stories.headline: At least 25 court cases in England and Wales hit by undisclosed AI use this year
stories.dek: Judges have flagged AI-written witness statements, invented case law and nonexistent laws, according to a count of published judgments by the Bureau of Investigative Journalism.
stories.summary: At least 25 court cases in England and Wales in 2026 were affected by undisclosed AI use, including invented rulings and an AI-written police statement. Senior legal figures have warned of the risks, and a judicial body has proposed new declarations for witnesses.
body: At least 25 court cases in England and Wales this year have been affected by undisclosed use of artificial intelligence, according to a count of published judgments by the Bureau of Investigative Journalism shared with The Guardian.

The cases matter because courts rely on lawyers and witnesses giving true, checked information. Judges have had to deal with AI-written witness statements, made-up case law and laws that do not exist. The Law Society's president said AI-generated paperwork is also eating into judges' time as courts try to clear backlogs.

The problems are often called "hallucinations": AI tools producing confident answers that are false. In a High Court dispute between tax lawyers, the judge called the use of such material "unacceptable". In a $21m (£16m) High Court case between two Nigerian oil companies, a barrister relied on a ruling attributed to a senior judge that an AI had invented. The judge warned of "the dangers of relying on the product of AI without verification".

In another case, senior insolvency judge Mark Mullen found a junior solicitor had used an AI chatbot to research a point of law and quoted a fictitious statute. He examined the chat logs and found the tool had produced "nonsense". He wrote that "AI has the potential to be wholly unreliable".

The Court of Appeal dismissed an application by a Derbyshire man who wanted to challenge a four-year sentence for offences including grievous bodily harm. The investigating police officer had uploaded a transcript of the victim's interviews to Microsoft's Copilot and asked it to produce a victim personal statement that would achieve "the highest sentence" and make a judge "weep". The officer was removed from frontline duty. The judges said no police officer should ever prepare a witness statement of any kind in this way.

Earlier this month a Crown Prosecution Service lawyer cited an imaginary legal precedent. Many affected cases involved people representing themselves, but lawyers are also using AI to speed up research and increase earnings, the investigation found.

Brett Dixon, president of the Law Society, said a self-represented person using commercial AI can turn "three pages from a lawyer" into "a rambling 60 pages". Supreme Court judge Lord Sales said last week that the court was growing "increasingly concerned". He said the greater long-term danger is that people "gradually lose the ability to know whether it has got the answer wrong".

Last month the Civil Justice Council recommended that witnesses of fact in civil cases sign a declaration that AI did not generate or influence the substance of their statements. Its working group, led by Sir Colin Birss, also called for urgent guidance for people representing themselves.
A Ministry of Justice spokesperson said the government is aware of the growing use of AI in courts and is taking steps to ensure it is "safe, appropriate, and properly controlled".
keyFacts: The Bureau of Investigative Journalism counted at least 25 affected cases in 2026 from published judgments.
The Civil Justice Council's working group is led by Sir Colin Birss.
A police officer was removed from frontline duty after using Copilot for a victim statement.
The Nigerian oil companies' High Court dispute is worth $21m (£16m).
stories.background: Generative AI tools such as chatbots write text in response to prompts but can state falsehoods, including citing court rulings that never existed. Courts in England and Wales rely on lawyers to check authorities before citing them. Senior judges and legal bodies have issued warnings about the technology in recent years.

stories.headline: Google to publish Android developers' phone numbers and addresses from March 1
stories.dek: Developers who earn money from apps in the UK or Europe must declare themselves traders by February 1, 2027, and Google will show their contact details worldwide.
stories.summary: Google will publicly list the phone number and address of Android developers who declare themselves traders under UK and European law, starting March 1. Independent developers say the rule threatens their privacy, as Google will show the details worldwide.
body: Google will start publishing the phone numbers and addresses of many Android app developers on March 1, 2027, under rules meant to meet the European Union's Digital Services Act.

The change affects independent developers who work from home. Many may have to put a home address online or pay for another way to provide a business address. Google says the details will be public worldwide, not only in Europe.

Developers have until February 1, 2027 to declare whether they are a "trader" under UK and European law. Google says the term broadly applies to anyone who earns revenue from apps, especially if the revenue is regular or high in volume.

Developers are exempt if their apps are a hobby or non-commercial, or if they do not publish them in the UK or Europe. Those who declare themselves traders will have their contact details shown from March 1.

Google does not accept PO box addresses for developer payment profiles. Developers without an office must therefore either share a home address or pay for a registered agent or similar service that supplies a business address.
One independent developer told The Elec they were considering renting a private office only to comply with the rules.

Apple is subject to the same regulations but is handling them differently. It will show developer addresses only within the relevant European countries. It also allows PO box addresses if the developer gives Apple a receipt or bill linking the box to their regular address.
The Verge said it had asked Google why PO boxes are not allowed and why details are being shared globally. Google had not replied when the report was published.
keyFacts: Developers must declare trader status by February 1, 2027.
Contact details go public from March 1, 2027.
Google does not accept PO boxes for developer payment profile addresses.
Apple will show developer addresses only in the relevant European countries.
Hobby and non-commercial developers, and those not publishing in the UK or Europe, are exempt.
stories.background: The Digital Services Act is a European Union law that sets rules for online platforms. Under it, platforms must make certain traders' contact details available to users. Google and Apple, which run the main app stores, are both covered.
stories.whatNext: Developers must declare whether they are traders by February 1, 2027, and Google will begin publishing contact details on March 1.

stories.headline: BJP and JD(S) agree to contest Karnataka local body polls and bypolls together
stories.dek: Leaders of both parties also decided to set up state and district coordination committees, with the state panel expected within four days.
stories.summary: The BJP and JD(S) decided at a meeting in Bengaluru on Thursday to fight all coming elections together, including panchayat and municipal polls and two Assembly bypolls. Union Minister H D Kumaraswamy said an NDA candidate will contest the Hiriyur bypoll.
body: The BJP and the JD(S) decided on Thursday to contest all upcoming elections in Karnataka together, including panchayat and municipal polls and by-elections to Assembly seats.
The decision affects voters in the coming local body elections and in the two Assembly constituencies where bypolls are due. Leaders of both parties met in Bengaluru to settle the approach.

The parties also decided to form coordination committees at state and district levels to strengthen the alliance at the grassroots. The state-level committee is likely to be formed in the next four days. It is likely to have five BJP members and four from the JD(S).

District panels will select candidates and prepare for the panchayat elections. A senior JD(S) leader said their make-up would depend on each party's strength in the district. "The BJP is stronger in some districts, while the JD(S) has a more dominant presence in others," he said, adding that the stronger party would have more representation.

Union Minister H D Kumaraswamy said the alliance was meant to last. "We will work together to dislodge the Congress from power," he said. He pointed to the NDA's performance in the recent Council elections and said, "The results clearly show that people are in favour of the alliance."
Kumaraswamy said an NDA candidate would contest the Hiriyur bypoll and that both parties would work together for the alliance's win.

R Ashoka, the Leader of the Opposition in the Assembly, said the meeting discussed electoral strategy for the two bypolls and the local body polls. He said central leaders would be consulted and candidates finalised. Karnataka BJP president B Y Vijayendra and other senior leaders of both parties attended.

Those at the meeting said the BJP central leadership is likely to be consulted and a seat-sharing formula agreed for the local body polls before the Winter Session of the legislature begins in Belagavi.

Ashoka also urged the government to extend the Winter Session to 15 days so that issues of North Karnataka can be discussed in detail. The opposition is likely to raise the NICE project scam, the proposed Bidadi township, the KPSC recruitment scam, delayed payment of Rs 2,500 to drought-hit farmers and the denial of Gruha Lakshmi benefits for three months.

stories.headline: Governor Arlekar asks CM Vijay to help fill vice-chancellor posts in Tamil Nadu universities
stories.dek: In a letter, the Governor proposed a four-member search committee and a fixed timeline for appointments, and asked for a schedule to hold pending convocations.
stories.summary: Tamil Nadu Governor Rajendra Arlekar has written to Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay seeking his personal help in naming full-time vice-chancellors. He proposed a four-member selection panel and a time-bound process; 19 of 22 state universities have no vice-chancellor.
body: Tamil Nadu Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar has asked Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay to step in personally to appoint vice-chancellors for state universities and to hold convocations that are overdue.

Of the 22 state universities, 19 are running without a vice-chancellor. Arlekar said thousands of students waiting for their degrees are losing out. The letter is dated November 25, and Lok Bhavan, the Governor's office, issued a release on Thursday.

Arlekar said that without full-time vice-chancellors, administration and academic work have suffered. Decisions are now made through a convenor committee set up by the state government. In his view, that body has not managed to handle what each university needs from day to day, because such needs call for decisions at the level of the institution.

He said the main disagreement between the state government and the Chancellor, a post the Governor holds, is the make-up of the search-cum-selection committees. The question is whether a nominee of the University Grants Commission (UGC) chairman should sit on them under Regulation 7.3(ii) of the UGC Regulations, 2018. The differing positions have led to court proceedings.

Arlekar cited a Supreme Court judgment of January 30, 2026, in Dr S Mohan v. Secretary to the Chancellor, Puducherry Technological University. He also referred to a release of February 2, 2026, by the then Governor, RN Ravi. It asked for a UGC nominee on search committees and for ongoing selection proceedings to be kept on hold until the court cases were decided.

To end the deadlock, Arlekar proposed a four-member committee with one nominee each of the Chancellor, the university syndicate, the UGC chairman and the state government. This would be subject to statutory provisions and court directions. Members should be distinguished academicians and experts of proven integrity, he said.

He also proposed a timeline. The committee should start preferably six months before an expected vacancy and advertise the post within 15 days of being formed. Scrutiny and interviews should be done within two months of the advertisement. It should then agree unanimously on three eligible candidates and rank them in order of preference.
He also suggested a university-wise schedule to hold all pending convocations at the earliest, wherever legally permissible.

"I am confident that through mutual consultation and cooperation, an early and legally sustainable resolution can be achieved," Arlekar said in the letter. The state government had not publicly responded.
keyFacts: Arlekar's letter to Chief Minister Vijay is dated November 25.
19 of Tamil Nadu's 22 state universities have no vice-chancellor.
The proposed panel would have nominees of the Chancellor, syndicate, UGC chairman and state government.
Posts should be advertised within 15 days of the committee being formed.
The Governor wants the committee to shortlist and rank three candidates unanimously.
stories.background: The Governor is the Chancellor of state universities. The state government and the Chancellor have differed over whether a UGC chairman's nominee should be on vice-chancellor search committees. The dispute has led to court proceedings, and a government-appointed convenor committee now oversees the universities' administration.

stories.summary: The Madras High Court has ordered the Chennai Collector and the commissioners of the Greater Chennai Corporation and Greater Chennai Police to appear on December 1. The contempt case concerns encroachments on Loop Road at Marina Beach.
body: The Madras High Court has ordered the Chennai Collector and the commissioners of the Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) and Greater Chennai Police (GCP) to appear before it on December 1 in a contempt case over encroachments on Loop Road at Marina Beach.
Contempt of court means failing to follow a court's order. The case concerns whether authorities kept Loop Road clear, which matters to people who drive along or live near the Marina.
A division bench of Justices AG Jagadish Chandira and Shamim Ahmed passed the order on Tuesday. M Anand of Nochikuppam in Chennai had filed an application in the matter, and the bench was hearing it.
The bench recalled that in an order dated February 17, 2025, it had ended a case it had started on its own motion. It did so after the additional advocate general made a submission to the court.
At that time, the court directed the GCC and the GCP to make sure at all times that nothing blocks the smooth flow of traffic on Loop Road.

stories.headline: Delhi HC issues notice to JNU on student union plea over PhD reservation
stories.dek: The Jawaharlal Nehru University Students' Union says the 2026–27 PhD prospectus left out seats for SC, ST and disabled candidates. The next hearing is on December 18.
stories.summary: The Delhi High Court on Thursday issued notice to JNU on a students' union petition alleging reservation rules were not followed in the 2026–27 PhD prospectus. The court has sought the university's response, and the case returns on December 18.
body: The Delhi High Court on Thursday issued notice to Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) on a petition alleging that its PhD prospectus for the 2026–27 session violates reservation rules.

The petition was filed by the Jawaharlal Nehru University Students' Union (JNUSU). It was listed for its first hearing on November 26. The court has asked the JNU administration to respond to the issues raised, JNUSU said.

The union alleges that the prospectus leaves out seats for Scheduled Caste (SC), Scheduled Tribe (ST) and Persons with Disabilities (PwD) candidates. The matter affects PhD applicants in those categories, who are entitled to reserved seats under statutory norms.

JNUSU said it would keep pressing for accountability and for corrective steps to make sure the reservation rules are followed. It said it would oppose the continuation of the viva voce, the interview stage of admission, unless the prospectus is advertised again with the prescribed reservations.

The union also raised concern over a delay in NET interviews, which it said has caused distress among PhD aspirants. It demanded that the university immediately re-advertise the seats it says are missing and restart the admission process at the earliest.

JNUSU said the process must protect the rights of SC, ST and PwD candidates and must not dilute or deny reservation provisions. The university's position was not stated in the reports of Thursday's hearing.
keyFacts: The Delhi High Court issued notice to JNU on Thursday, November 26.
The petition was filed by the Jawaharlal Nehru University Students' Union.
It concerns the PhD prospectus for the 2026–27 academic session.
The next hearing is scheduled for December 18.
stories.background: JNU is a public research university in Delhi, established in 1969. Reservation in admissions for SC, ST and PwD candidates is governed by statutory norms, which the students' union says the PhD prospectus does not follow.

stories.headline: Cyberabad civic body suspends official after green tanker filled from drain
stories.dek: The corporation also cancelled the contractor's work order after an online post claimed tankers meant to carry treated wastewater were being loaded at drains.
stories.summary: The Cyberabad Municipal Corporation suspended a circle manager and cancelled a contractor's work order after an online post claimed Green Water Tankers were filled at drains, not treatment plants. The body said it would step up monitoring.
body: The Cyberabad Municipal Corporation (CMC) has suspended Vikram Chandra, a circle manager, after allegations that a Green Water Tanker was filled with untreated drain water instead of treated water.
The tankers supply treated wastewater for construction and other uses that do not involve drinking. The quality of that water matters to builders and residents who rely on it.
CMC Commissioner G Srijana ordered the suspension. Chandra is the Circle Manager for Serilingampally and is in charge of the Narsingi and Patancheru circles.
The corporation has also identified Gopal, an outsourcing supervisor, for action. The work order of the contractor concerned has been cancelled.

The action followed a post on social media. It claimed that tankers meant to carry treated wastewater were being loaded straight from drains, and it raised doubts about the water being sold for non-drinking use.

The CMC said that only properly treated water from sewage treatment plants (STPs) must be supplied through Green Water Tankers, and only for designated non-potable uses. It said monitoring would be strengthened and action taken against violations.

Outsourcing supervisor Gopal has been identified for action.
The contractor's work order has been cancelled.

stories.headline: Kerala CM orders inquiry into caste discrimination against Chakkliya families in Idukki
stories.dek: Chief Minister V D Satheesan asked the district collector for a report on alleged bans on water use in Koviloor village, Vattavada panchayat.
stories.summary: Chief Minister V D Satheesan on Thursday ordered an inquiry into alleged caste discrimination against Chakkliya families in Idukki. The allegations include an unofficial ban on their use of common water sources in Koviloor village.
body: Kerala Chief Minister V D Satheesan on Thursday ordered the Idukki district collector to investigate alleged caste discrimination against Chakkliya families and submit a report.

The order concerns Koviloor village in Vattavada panchayat. Chakkliya families there are alleged to face social exclusion, including an unofficial ban on using common water sources and washing clothes at them.

The Chief Minister's Office said Satheesan asked K A Thulasi, the minister for Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe and Backward Classes Welfare, to take immediate steps. In a social media post, he said he had also told the minister to ensure caste discrimination does not occur anywhere in the state.
The families are also alleged to lack adequate drinking water at home and to face restrictions when they try to collect water from local streams.

"At a time when the world is exploring the limitless possibilities of advanced technologies, including artificial intelligence, the reality that an age-old practice from centuries ago continues to prevail in Koviloor has come to light," Satheesan said. "The continued existence of untouchability in the name of caste is a disgrace to our society."

Vattavada panchayat has around 270 Chakkiliyan families, who live alongside dominant communities such as the Mannadiar, Chettiyar and Maravar. Residents have faced untouchability over generations, including being barred from entering private homes and compounds. Tea stalls used separate glasses for different castes until the practice was abolished in 1991 after public campaigns.

Barbershops also refused to serve Chakkiliyan residents, who had to travel up to 42 kilometres to Munnar or 12 kilometres to Ellapetty for a haircut. In August 2020, the panchayat cancelled the licences of two salons that discriminated. It then set up a caste-neutral salon in a local body building, run by a barber named Bhagyaraj.

That salon is now in doubt. The government audit wing objected to the rent-free arrangement because minutes of the panchayat meeting approving it were missing. Officials have demanded rent of ₹5,000 a month plus arrears, which the barber cannot pay as the shop mainly serves Chakkliya residents. Local administrators have asked the state government to waive the rent, warning that closure could revive discrimination.
keyFacts: Vattavada panchayat has around 270 Chakkiliyan families.
Tea stalls' double-glass system for separating castes was abolished in 1991.
The panchayat cancelled two discriminating salons' licences in August 2020.
Officials have demanded ₹5,000 monthly rent from the caste-neutral salon, plus arrears.
stories.background: Chakkliya families in Vattavada have faced untouchability for generations. After the panchayat cancelled the licences of two discriminating salons in 2020, a community-run, caste-neutral salon opened in a local body building.
stories.whatNext: The Idukki district collector is to submit a report on the allegations; no date was given.

stories.headline: BMC house leader alleges mangrove destruction in Gorai and Dahisar, seeks probe
stories.dek: Ganesh Khankar asked for a 10-year satellite imagery audit and said he would go to court if the civic administration does not act.
stories.summary: BMC Leader of the House Ganesh Khankar alleged at the Standing Committee meeting on Thursday that mangroves in Gorai and Dahisar are being destroyed by debris dumping. He demanded a probe and a satellite audit, and said he may go to court.
body: Ganesh Khankar, the Leader of the House in the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC), alleged at Thursday's Standing Committee meeting that mangroves and creek land in Gorai and Dahisar are being destroyed, and warned of an environmental disaster.

Mangroves are coastal trees that protect the shoreline and absorb floodwater. Khankar said unchecked landfilling could push Mumbai into serious environmental harm. He said he would approach the court with satellite images as evidence if the administration did not take the matter seriously.

Raising a point of order, he alleged that construction debris was being dumped openly to reclaim and occupy mangrove land in the Borivali-Gorai creek belt. He said he had photographs and claimed 110 to 150 truckloads of debris were dumped every day.

Khankar alleged that mangroves spread over hundreds of acres, in an area running from Charkop to Ganpat Patil Nagar and on to Kandarpada in Dahisar, were being cleared. He said cricket turfs, badminton courts, furniture warehouses and marriage halls were coming up on the reclaimed land.
He said the issue had earlier been raised in the presence of Union Minister Piyush Goyal, with photographs submitted and an inquiry sought. Civic officials, he alleged, did not act.

Khankar accused BMC officials and senior police personnel of a possible nexus with those behind the reclamation and demanded a probe. He also sought a 10-year satellite imagery audit of the stretch from Link Road and Charkop to Ganpat Patil Nagar, with a comparison of the past two years and the present.
He said failure to act could again take Municipal Commissioner Ashwini Bhide to court, after a recent judicial reprimand in the Magathane bus depot case in Borivali.

Khankar also questioned what he called double standards. BMC's own projects, he said, face months of delay and repeated follow-ups to get Coastal Regulation Zone clearances, while mangrove and creek land is allegedly being filled in openly without intervention.
The civic administration and the police have not responded to the allegations.
keyFacts: Khankar claimed 110 to 150 truckloads of debris are dumped daily in the area.
He named Charkop, Ganpat Patil Nagar and Kandarpada in Dahisar as affected areas.
He sought a 10-year satellite imagery audit of the coastal stretch.
He said he earlier raised the issue in the presence of Union Minister Piyush Goyal.
stories.background: Mangroves along Mumbai's creeks are covered by Coastal Regulation Zone rules, which require clearances for work near the coast. Khankar referred to a recent court reprimand of Municipal Commissioner Ashwini Bhide in the Magathane bus depot case in Borivali.

stories.headline: Wife of Japanese journalist held in Russia appeals for his release
stories.dek: Nozomi Imai said in her first public statement that her husband Yuki Imai, a Hokkaido Shimbun reporter, is a son, husband and father, and asked for help securing his freedom.
stories.summary: Nozomi Imai, wife of Hokkaido Shimbun reporter Yuki Imai, pleaded on Thursday for his release from detention in Moscow on suspicion of spying. Russia accuses him of collecting information on its defence capabilities; his employer and Japan's prime minister deny this.
body: The wife of Japanese journalist Yuki Imai, who is held in Moscow on suspicion of espionage, publicly appealed on Thursday for his release.
The case adds strain to relations between Japan and Russia, which have worsened since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 and Japan's decision to join sanctions on Moscow.

Imai, 34, is a reporter for the Hokkaido Shimbun newspaper. He was detained in mid-October as he prepared to return home from a two-year posting in Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk, on Sakhalin island in Russia's far east. Russian authorities allege he collected information on Russian defence capabilities. The newspaper has said he was doing ordinary news gathering and that it does not report on government instructions. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has said: "There is no such fact."

His wife, Nozomi Imai, 32, issued the statement through the newspaper in Japanese, English and Russian. It was her first public comment since the arrest. She did not address the allegations and declined to comment further.

She said she could hardly breathe when she saw television footage of her husband with his arms bound behind his back. Souvenirs he had bought for the family were visible in his suitcase. "I could not sleep even for a moment that night," she said.

The couple's daughter is 21 months old and was born during his posting. Nozomi Imai said the child has learnt many new words since she last saw her father in September. "Sometimes she looks down the dark hallway and says, 'Papa's not here,'" she said.

She said his elderly parents fear they may never see their son again. She added that doctors say his mother is at risk of a brain haemorrhage. "Please, please return this precious papa to his little daughter," she said.

The newspaper said Imai's grandfather was born on Sakhalin and that Imai admired Russian culture and promoted grassroots exchanges. His wife said they met as students through a shared love of Russian films and novels.

Japanese diplomats have seen Imai twice. Ambassador Akira Muto met him at Lefortovo detention centre in Moscow this week and said he appeared to be in good health. Lawyers appointed by his employer have also met him.

Takaichi raised the case with Russian President Vladimir Putin at last week's Apec summit in China and asked for Imai's release. Russia's Federal Security Service, which is investigating, has not commented publicly since announcing the arrest.
Interfax news agency reported that Imai will stay at Lefortovo for at least two months while prosecutors consider the case. It said a conviction for espionage could bring 10 to 20 years in prison.
keyFacts: Yuki Imai is 34; his wife Nozomi is 32.
Their daughter is 21 months old and was born during his Sakhalin posting.
Japanese diplomats have visited Imai twice, including Ambassador Akira Muto this week.
Kyodo reported his current detention period runs to December 12 but could be extended.
Interfax said espionage convictions can carry 10 to 20 years in prison.
stories.background: Japan and Russia have long disputed four islands in the Kuril chain, which Russia administers and Japan claims as the Northern Territories. Ties worsened after Japan joined sanctions over the 2022 invasion of Ukraine. Moscow this month also seized the Russian assets of Japan Tobacco, which is partly owned by the Japanese government. Reuters described Imai's arrest as the most high-profile detention of a foreign journalist in Russia since Wall Street Journal reporter Evan Gershkovich in 2023.
stories.whatNext: Imai's current detention is due to expire on December 12 but could be extended, Kyodo news agency said.

stories.headline: Ramayana crosses ₹990 crore in India on day 22, nears ₹1,000 crore mark
stories.dek: Nitesh Tiwari's film earned ₹9.65 crore on Thursday, while two new releases compete with it for screens and show slots this weekend.
stories.summary: Ramayana, starring Ranbir Kapoor and Yash, has collected ₹992.10 crore in India after 22 days, according to Sacnilk figures. Two new films, Yeh Prem Mol Liya and Gunmaaster G9, open on Friday and are competing with it for shows.
body: Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana earned ₹9.65 crore in India on Thursday, its 22nd day, taking its total to ₹992.10 crore, according to figures from the tracking site Sacnilk.
The film has been in theatres since November 5. The ₹1,000 crore mark in India is now within reach, and Hindustan Times expects the film to cross it by Friday.

Thursday's figure was a small rise on Wednesday's ₹9.50 crore. Another trade tracker, Pinkvilla, estimated Wednesday's collection at ₹8.50 crore, a 48 per cent fall from Tuesday. Its running total on Wednesday was ₹947.25 crore net, including 3D charges. The two outlets' figures differ because they are separate estimates and are not certified accounts.

Ramayana opened at ₹64.85 crore on its first day, the fourth-highest opening in Bollywood history. It crossed ₹500 crore within six days, helped by the Diwali holidays. Collections dipped in the third week. The makers then cut ticket prices, and many halls now sell Ramayana tickets for as little as ₹99.

The film has collected over ₹1700 crore gross worldwide, and is the second-highest-grossing Hindi film in India. Its makers are hoping to pass the all-time record held by Dangal with releases planned in China, Japan and South Korea. Pinkvilla said releases in China, Japan, Korea and Russia are slated for 2027.

Pinkvilla also said the film did not do as well in the Hindi heartland as trade expected, and called its run an underperformance against those hopes. It projected a global finish near ₹1850 crore net for the first phase.

Meanwhile, Ayushmann Khurrana and Sharvari's Yeh Prem Mol Liya and Emraan Hashmi's Gunmaaster G9 open on Friday. Bollywood Hungama reported that bookings had not opened at many single-screen and two-screen cinemas in Mumbai as of 9 am on Thursday.

A trade source told the outlet that Ramayana's distributors had also asked single screens for a show, as the film is still doing well and fourth-weekend advance booking is encouraging. Most single screens can run five shows a day at most, and Yeh Prem Mol Liya runs 2 hours and 53 minutes, against 2 hours and 22 minutes for Gunmaaster G9.
MovieMax Andheri has chosen to give two shows each to the new films and keep one for Ramayana. Nishat in Grant Road will run only Gunmaaster G9, with four shows a day.
Ramayana has also made two technical shortlists for the 32nd Annual Critics Choice Awards, for Best Visual Effects and Best Stunt Design. The second part is set for Diwali 2028.
keyFacts: Ramayana opened at ₹64.85 crore in India on November 5.
Many cinemas now sell Ramayana tickets for as low as ₹99.

Part two of Ramayana is set for Diwali 2028.

stories.background: Ramayana is a two-part adaptation of Valmiki's epic, directed by Nitesh Tiwari. Ranbir Kapoor plays Rama, Sai Pallavi plays Sita, Yash plays Ravana and Sunny Deol plays Hanuman. It is produced by Namit Malhotra's Prime Focus Studios with DNEG and Yash's Monster Mind Creations.

stories.headline: Shah Rukh Khan's legal team says defamation notice to influencer was not issued by him
stories.dek: Hirani Associates said the notice dated November 23, which named content creator Suvigya Sharma, was not sent by the actor or on his behalf, and asked media to correct reports.
stories.summary: Shah Rukh Khan's lawyers, Hirani Associates, said a defamation notice circulating online was not issued by the actor or on his behalf. The notice had been linked to a viral Instagram Reel about an event interaction involving Anant Ambani and Sadhguru.
body: Shah Rukh Khan's lawyers, Hirani Associates, said on Thursday that a defamation notice attributed to the actor and addressed to a content creator was not issued by him or on his behalf.

The notice had been widely reported as legal action against Suvigya Sharma, who runs the Instagram handle @ram.bhakt.suvi. The firm asked media houses and social media pages to check facts before reporting and to correct or remove posts that tie the notice to Khan.

In a statement shared on Instagram Stories, the firm said: "A purported 'legal notice' dated 23 November 2026, said to have been issued on behalf of Mr. Shah Rukh Khan, is being circulated on social media and in some news reports. As authorised attorneys of Mr. Shah Rukh Khan, we clarify that this notice was not issued by him or on his behalf. Mr. Khan has not instructed any advocate or law firm, including us, to issue it."

The row began when Sharma posted a Reel from the Global Peace Honours 2026. It showed an interaction between Khan, Anant Ambani and spiritual leader Sadhguru. In his commentary, Sharma alleged that Khan had been asked to "remain silent".

Screenshots of a notice dated November 23 then appeared online. Deccan Herald reported on Thursday that Khan had sent it. That report said the notice called the Reel "mischievous, misleading and defamatory" and cited Section 356 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, which deals with defamation.
The notice set a 48-hour deadline. It asked Sharma to remove the Reel, stop sharing the claim, correct the captions and confirm in writing what he had done.

Sharma posted a follow-up Reel about the notice. He said: "So, the man who allegedly told Shah Rukh Khan to shut up did not insult him? Or Shah Rukh Khan does not have the courage to say that he was insulted?" Sharma, who says he is a lawyer, also argued that his remarks were criticism protected by freedom of expression.
The law firm's statement did not say who produced the document. Khan's film King, directed by Siddharth Anand, is due in theatres on December 24.
keyFacts: The notice in question is dated November 23, 2026 and cites Section 356 of the BNS.
It set a 48-hour deadline and asked for removal of the Reel.
Hirani Associates posted its denial on Instagram Stories on Thursday, November 26.
Khan's film King, directed by Siddharth Anand, is slated for release on December 24.

stories.headline: Netflix announces Sukesh Chandrashekhar documentary, to stream from December 18
stories.dek: The film, produced by India Today Originals, draws on more than two years of research into the fraud and extortion cases linked to Chandrashekhar.
stories.summary: Netflix announced on Thursday a true-crime documentary titled Love Scam Aur Dhokha: The Sukesh Chandrashekhar Story, set to premiere on December 18. It looks at the allegations against Chandrashekhar, including claims that he ran a network of deception from Tihar jail.
body: Netflix announced on Thursday that its documentary Love Scam Aur Dhokha: The Sukesh Chandrashekhar Story will premiere on the streaming platform on December 18, the company said in a statement.
The film is about a man accused in several multi-crore fraud and extortion cases. The cases are still before the courts, and the allegations have not been established.

India Today Originals has produced the documentary. It is directed by Moumita Sen and Niyantha Shekar, with Karan Rana as co-director and Chandni Ahlawat Dabas as executive producer. Munish Pandey and Shams Tahir Khan are the crime consultants.
According to Netflix, the film traces Chandrashekhar's path from his early years in Bengaluru to the cases that brought him national attention. It draws on more than two years of research.

It also examines how he allegedly kept his operations going while held in Delhi's Tihar jail, and what gaps in the system may have allowed that. The makers say it looks at why influential people continued to believe his claims.

The case at the centre of the film involves allegations of an extortion of around ₹200 crore. Hindustan Times reported that, in the case, Chandrashekhar is alleged to have posed as a senior government official and taken the money from Aditi Singh, wife of former Ranbaxy promoter Shivinder Mohan Singh, during 2020-21. He is alleged to have promised to secure her husband's release from jail. Delhi Police's Economic Offences Wing filed a chargesheet under the Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act. Hindustan Times reported that he was sentenced to eight years in prison in the case.

His links with film personalities have also drawn attention. Actors Jacqueline Fernandez and Nora Fatehi have both said they knew nothing of his alleged criminal activities. Fatehi told the court she met him for the first time in December 2020 at an event organised by his associate Leena Maria Paul.

In June, a Delhi court directed that charges be framed against Fernandez, saying there was sufficient prima facie material that she received gifts from Chandrashekhar despite knowing of his criminal activities. Fernandez has maintained that she was a victim, not a willing participant.
The documentary comes from the makers of two earlier Netflix titles, Curry & Cyanide: The Jolly Joseph Case and The Indrani Mukerjea Story: Buried Truth.

The same makers produced Curry & Cyanide: The Jolly Joseph Case.

stories.headline: Astronomers find most distant quasar yet, seen 630 million years after Big Bang
stories.dek: The object's black hole already had about 360 million times the mass of the sun, which the lead researcher said raises the question of how it grew so fast.
stories.summary: A German-led team has identified the most distant quasar known, seen as it was 630 million years after the Big Bang. It beats the previous record by nearly 40 million years, according to lead researcher Julien Wolf.
body: A German-led team of astronomers reported on Tuesday that it has found the most distant quasar known, one that formed within 630 million years of the Big Bang.

A quasar is the very bright core of a galaxy, powered by a black hole that is pulling in gas. This one is seen as it was 13.1 billion years ago, when the universe was less than 5% of its present age. The universe is 13.8 billion years old.

Julien Wolf of the European Southern Observatory, who led the study, said the previous two records each moved the frontier back by about 15 million years or less. "This one takes us back by nearly 40 million years, the biggest advance in nearly a decade!" he said in an email.

The team found the object while searching millions of observations from the European Space Agency's Euclid telescope. Euclid was launched in 2023 and is surveying galaxies to learn more about dark matter and dark energy, which are linked to the expansion of the universe.
Wolf said finding a quasar this early is rare. He said this one is rarer still because its black hole is very large even though it feeds slowly on the material around it.

The Hubble and Webb space telescopes, along with other observatories on the ground and in space, corroborated the findings. Webb data showed the black hole has a mass equal to 360 million suns. The results are published in the journal Astronomy & Astrophysics.

Wolf nicknamed the quasar Dun Aonghasa, after a prehistoric stone fort in Ireland's Aran Islands that he visited with his Irish wife and daughter. He described the fort as a frontier holding "the promise of a vast horizon still to explore".
"About 630 million years after the Big Bang, its black hole had already grown to about 360 million times the mass of the sun. But how?" Wolf said.
He said the search continues. "Honestly, the record could fall again in a few months or it could stand for years," he said.
keyFacts: The quasar is catalogued at a redshift of z = 8.13, according to the paper's title.
Its black hole has a mass of about 360 million suns, measured with the Webb telescope.
Light from the quasar left it 13.1 billion years ago.
The paper, led by J. Wolf and S. Belladitta, appears in Astronomy & Astrophysics.
The previous two records each moved back about 15 million years or less.
stories.background: Quasars are a brief phase in a galaxy's life, when gas falling into a central supermassive black hole makes the core outshine the rest of the galaxy. They are bright enough to be seen across billions of light-years, which lets astronomers study the early universe.

stories.headline: Tom Hanks praises Maharaja actor Sachana Namidass: 'what an incredible actor'
stories.dek: Sachana Namidass, who won a National Award for playing Vijay Sethupathi's daughter, said hearing Hanks speak about her felt like a dream.
stories.summary: Hollywood actor Tom Hanks praised Sachana Namidass's performance in the 2024 Tamil film Maharaja, according to a television academy board member who spoke to him. Namidass called the praise a dream in an Instagram Story.
body: Hollywood actor Tom Hanks has praised Sachana Namidass's performance in the Tamil thriller Maharaja, according to Kavita Gupta, a board member of the International Academy of Television Arts & Sciences.
Namidass played Jothi, the daughter of Vijay Sethupathi's character, in the 2024 film. She won the National Film Award for Best Supporting Actress for the role. The film is on Netflix.

Gupta described the exchange in an interview with The Hollywood Reporter India. She said she met Hanks at a LACMA gala earlier this year, and he asked her which three Indian films he should watch. She told him to watch Maharaja.

She met him again on November 7 at the second LACMA Art+Film Gala. "The first thing he said to me was, 'I still can't get over that girl... what an incredible actor. I don't think I can do it; I would've killed the guy!'" Gupta said.
Namidass responded on Instagram Stories. "Still can't believe this happened. Hearing Tom Hanks talk about me and my journey feels like a dream," she wrote.
She also thanked the film's director, Nithilan Saminathan. "I'll always be grateful that you gave me the opportunity to be a part of Maharaja," she wrote.
Maharaja follows a barber in Chennai who goes to the police to report that his dustbin has been stolen. The case turns dark as the investigation goes on. Anurag Kashyap plays the antagonist.

Producer Sudhan Sundaram of Passion Studios has said a Hollywood agency acquired the remake rights after the film did well in China and on streaming. He said the agency is trying to set up the project with an A-list star, and that the film is likely to go on floors by next year.

Sundaram said that actor Matthew McConaughey may be one of the stars the agency is talking to, but that only the agency could confirm it. Sethupathi has said he would like a role in the remake and that a sequel, Maharaja 2, is in development.
keyFacts: Kavita Gupta says she met Hanks again on November 7 at the second LACMA Art+Film Gala.

stories.headline: Tamil Nadu renames Paraicheri village in Virudhunagar as Vadakku Achanthavilthan
stories.dek: The gazette notice directs authorities to correct records where the old name appears, including voter lists, bank records, Aadhaar and PAN cards.
stories.summary: A Virudhunagar District Gazette special issue dated 23 November 2026 renames Paraicheri village as Vadakku Achanthavilthan, South First reported. Authorities have been directed to correct their records; over 60 families had earlier described years of humiliation over the name.
body: The Tamil Nadu government has renamed Paraicheri village in Virudhunagar district as Vadakku Achanthavilthan, South First reported, citing a Virudhunagar District Gazette special issue dated 23 November 2026.
The old name is caste-based, and residents say it has long brought them ridicule. For people in the village, in Srivilliputhur taluk, the change also reaches official papers they use daily.

The notification cites G.O. No. G.O.1/587/2025, dated 19 November 2026. It says the decision followed a proposal from the district administration and recommendations from a committee set up to examine caste-based village names.

The notification lists the committee's members. They were the District Collector, the District Revenue Officer, the Sub-Collector, officials of the Adi Dravidar and Tribal Welfare Department, revenue officials, local body representatives and members of the public.

The notification directs the relevant authorities to make the necessary changes in their records. South First reported that the name Paraicheri had appeared on voter lists, bank records, Aadhaar and PAN cards. In land patta records, the village was officially recorded as Achanthavilthan.

South First had earlier reported that villagers boycotted the recent Tamil Nadu Assembly polls over the village's caste-based name. A photo caption in its report says billboards announcing a boycott of the 2026 elections had been put up in the village.
In that earlier reporting, over 60 families from the village said they had faced disrespect and humiliation for years because they belong to the Dalit community.

A Abi, a native of the village who is pursuing a PhD in Chennai, told South First how the name had affected her since childhood. She said she went to school in and around the village, and that for school she went to a neighbouring village where students from other communities also studied.
"They would mock us by calling out our village name, and even write it on classroom desks to ridicule us," she said.
South First's report does not carry a response from the district administration or the state government. It does not say when the records are to be corrected.
